patch.name: Machine room hum (loop)
patch.description: The plant room in the basement of an office block: a transformer humming at 100 Hz with its buzzing odd partials, a big extraction fan turning at 1500 rpm behind a grille, air pushing through the ducts, and every second or two a contactor clacking somewhere in a cabinet. Concrete walls, so everything is a little boxy. The extraction surges and eases once a loop: the ventilation swings from 0.3 to 0.6 of its range and back. A 4 s loop: the hum (50 Hz and its multiples) and the fan (25 turns a second) both fit a whole number of times, and the seam is crossfaded over 300 ms.

tracks.note: The transformer: mains hum at 100 Hz with strong 200, 300 and 400 Hz partials (so it is audible on small speakers) and a slow beat between its cores.

The extraction fan: an electric motor at 1500 rpm with seven blades, a soft drone and blade-passing flutter. Its level heaves in and out once per loop (the surge gain), as if the extraction were fighting a door opening somewhere.
Air in the sheet-metal ducts: steady noise ringing faintly in a long tube. The "room tone" between the tones. It surges with the fan.
Contactors in the switch cabinets: a hard plastic-and-metal clack now and then. They break up the drone and say "this place is running".

controls.label: Hum
controls.hint: A faint electrical presence to a transformer you feel in your teeth.

controls.label: Ventilation
controls.hint: Still air to a roaring extraction system.

controls.label: Surge
controls.hint: Steady air to an extraction that heaves in and out every four seconds.

controls.label: Activity
controls.hint: A plant ticking over at night to switchgear clacking constantly.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: A small cupboard of a room to a long concrete hall.

patch.name: Spaceship engine room (loop)
patch.description: The engine room of an old long-haul freighter under way: the reactor core throbs once every two seconds, a deep unstable tone that never quite repeats, the plasma conduits sing a slow swirling chord above it, coolant hisses through the pipes, and a status panel pings to itself in the corner. Steel walls, a tank of a room. An 8 s stereo loop; the throb and the swirl are tied to the loop length (0.5 and 0.125 Hz) and the seam is crossfaded over 1 s.

tracks.note: The reactor: a Lorenz attractor as a low tone that wanders between two states, driven hard, then swelling every 2 s (the throb comes after the drive, so the saturation cannot flatten it). Alive and slightly worrying.
The plasma conduits: a detuned FM chord with a slow phaser sweep, the "technology" above the rumble.
Coolant and air handling: a band of hiss that drifts, so the room has air in it.
A status panel: sparse, soft, high pings at slightly different pitches. Scale and a sign of life.

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: Drifting on standby to engines at full burn: higher, harder and brighter.

controls.label: Instability
controls.hint: A healthy, steady core to one that lurches and growls.

controls.label: Conduits
controls.hint: Bare rumble to a singing, swirling chord over it.

controls.label: Hull
controls.hint: A cramped crawlway to a cavernous steel hold.

controls.label: Systems
controls.hint: Dead consoles and still air to a busy, hissing, pinging room.

patch.name: Bird tweet
patch.description: A robin-sized songbird on a branch ten metres away, one phrase: four clear whistled notes that each swoop down and flick up (every 115 ms, drifting higher), then a fast dry trill of a dozen chips from 520 ms that tumbles down and stops at 800 ms. The wood answers softly.

tracks.note: The whistled notes: a nearly pure tone from the syrinx with a fast swoop in each note. The second voice of the syrinx adds a faint shimmer above.
The rattle that ends the phrase: quick falling chips at about 30 a second, the whole run sliding down a third.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A tiny wren to a blackbird: lower, rounder notes.

controls.label: Tempo
controls.hint: A lazy song to a hurried one.

controls.label: Melody
controls.hint: Every note the same, to a phrase that climbs and wanders.

controls.label: Trill
controls.hint: Whistles only, to a long rattle at the end.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: On your windowsill to far off in the wood.

patch.name: Critter chirp
patch.description: A palm-sized furry critter asking a question: two quick squeaks from a tiny throat, "pri-rip?", the second one higher and curling up at the end (0 and 130 ms, each about 90 ms), with a fast throat flutter, then a wet little sniff at 330 ms. Close, dry, in a burrow.

tracks.note: The voice: a tiny throat (size 0.42) squeaking twice. The pitch curve is the question mark; the flutter makes it furry, not a whistle.
A short wet sniff after the question: breath only, through the same small throat. Mute it and the critter is less alive.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A mouse-sized squeaker to a fat guinea pig: lower and rounder.

controls.label: Question
controls.hint: How far the second squeak jumps up: flat and bored to a startled "eep?".

controls.label: Flutter
controls.hint: The purring roll in the throat: a clean peep to a rolled "prrr".

controls.label: Sniff
controls.hint: The wet sniff after the squeaks, from none to a snuffly nose.

patch.name: Ghostly moan
patch.description: Something that used to be a person, sighing in an empty stone church: a breathy "oooh" with no chest in it that darkens through "ü" to a covered "ö", a cry that drops, rises once more and sinks away by 2.6 s, rough with a growl, and a second voice a little out of tune. A cold draught moans low through the stones beneath it. Most of what you hear is the building.

tracks.note: The voice: slack folds, half breath and a heavy growl that roughens it; the vowel darkens from "oo" through "ü" to a covered "ö". The slow vibrato that fades in is the sorrow.
Cold air through a gap: noise ringing in a narrow tube, low-passed with a little resonance near 500 Hz, so it moans low under the voice instead of whistling.

controls.label: Sorrow
controls.hint: A flat, empty sigh to a wailing lament: wider pitch arc and tremble.

controls.label: Voice
controls.hint: A lost child, a woman, to a hollow old man.

controls.label: Menace
controls.hint: A sorrowful sigh to a rough, growling throat.

controls.label: Breath
controls.hint: A sung tone to almost nothing but air.

controls.label: Draught
controls.hint: Still air to a cold wind moaning under the voice: louder, and less muffled as it grows.

controls.label: Beyond
controls.hint: In the room with you, to far away on the other side.

patch.name: Insect fly-by
patch.description: A fat bumblebee crossing in front of your face from left to right at five metres a second, passing 30 cm from the nose at 1.1 s: 170 wing beats a second, never quite steady, the buzz bending down as it passes and fading into the garden by 2.3 s. Stereo.

tracks.note: The wing beat: a narrow pulse wave that wanders in pitch and flutters in level as the insect corrects its flight, moved past the listener.
The papery rustle of the wings themselves: thin noise chopped at the wing rate, heard only when it is close.

controls.label: Insect
controls.hint: A whining mosquito, through a housefly, to a heavy bumblebee.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: Drifting past to zipping by: a bigger, quicker pitch drop.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Across the garden to brushing your ear.

controls.label: Nerves
controls.hint: A calm cruise to a frantic, zigzagging buzz.

patch.name: Kaiju roar
patch.description: A skyscraper-sized monster roaring over a city, made the way the classic one was: a resined glove dragged down a slack bass string, slowed down. A metallic shriek climbs for 400 ms, holds and wavers, then falls away over two seconds, on top of a chest roar an octave and more below it and a blast of air. The roar hits the far buildings and comes back 180 ms later.

tracks.note: The signature: a bowed, gritty string with a pitch arc, pushed through a giant mouth. This is what makes it a kaiju and not a lion.
The body under the shriek: a kaiju-sized throat growling at 50 to 70 Hz with harmonics up to 400 Hz so laptops still get the weight.
The air leaving a mouth the size of a bus: a noise swell that peaks with the shriek and outlasts it a little.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A dinosaur to a monster that blocks out the sky: everything drops and slows.

controls.label: Shriek
controls.hint: How much of the metallic scream rides on top: a deep bellow to a piercing screech.

controls.label: Rage
controls.hint: A tired call to a furious, distorted, air-blasting roar.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Standing under it to hearing it from across the bay: more city echo, less top.

patch.name: Monster growl
patch.description: A bear-sized beast warning you off from the back of its den: a chest-deep growl that swells for 300 ms, opens from "oo" to "ah" as the lips pull back around 600 ms, rattles there, then sinks and closes by 1.7 s. Hot breath hisses through the teeth the whole time. Heard from three metres in a rock chamber.

tracks.note: The growl itself: a big throat with period-doubled folds (growl) and a slow rattle in level. Pitch rises with the threat and sags at the end.
Air through wet teeth: pink noise shaped by the same mouth opening. It carries the growl on small speakers.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A big dog to something that fills the cave: deeper chest, longer throat.

controls.label: Anger
controls.hint: A low warning rumble to a torn, snarling threat with bared teeth.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A short grunt of a growl to a long drawn-out one.

controls.label: Den
controls.hint: Right at your ear to deep inside an echoing rock chamber.

patch.name: Robot creature chatter
patch.description: A knee-high maintenance droid with opinions: about 0.9 s of burbling electronic speech, a dozen syllables of unstable tone that jump in pitch like words, squeezed through a small plastic speaker-mouth, ending on a rising two-note "bee-woop?" at 950 ms. Its arms and head jerk about on little servos as it talks, and the head tilts as it finishes. Close, in a corridor.

tracks.note: The speech: two cross-modulating oscillators whose pitch is thrown to a new value 13 times a second, each syllable a little chaotic. Seeds change what it says.
The sign-off: two clean notes, the second sliding up. It turns noise into a sentence with a meaning.

Its arms and head jerking about while it talks: small servo moves scattered through the speech, each at its own moment, speed and strength (the seed decides). Low-passed, so they are darker and softer than the head tilt at the end.
The head tilting as it asks: a small geared motor, 160 ms. Gives the voice a body.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A pocket-sized bot to a barrel-shaped one: lower voice, bigger mouth.

controls.label: Talk speed
controls.hint: Slow, deliberate words to an excited gabble.

controls.label: Expression
controls.hint: A monotone drone to wild leaps of pitch.

controls.label: Glitch
controls.hint: A healthy clean voice to a damaged, crackling one.

controls.label: Servo
controls.hint: How loud its motors are: the twitches as it talks and the head tilt at the end.

controls.label: Fidget
controls.hint: Still while it talks to jerking about on every other word: from one servo twitch to seven.

patch.name: Slime squelch
patch.description: A fist-sized blob of slime dropping onto a stone floor and pulling itself together: a soft rubbery splat at 0, the wet suck of its skin peeling off the stone from 40 to 260 ms (a mouth-like "shhluck" that closes), and a dozen fat bubbles popping inside it until about 350 ms. Close, with no room around it.

tracks.note: The body landing: a dead rubber skin hit softly. No ring, only a round thump at 100 to 200 Hz.
The squelch: hundreds of tiny wet pops (drops, not hiss) through a small mouth that goes from open to closed, so it says "shluck". The vowel sweep is the stickiness; the drops are the wetness.
Air pockets popping in the goo: rising-pitch drops, biggest first. They make it thick liquid, not water.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A drip of goo to a bucket-sized blob: lower, fatter bubbles and a heavier splat.

controls.label: Stickiness
controls.hint: A quick wet slap to a long, reluctant peel.

controls.label: Bubbles
controls.hint: Smooth jelly to a fizzing, popping mass.

controls.label: Wetness
controls.hint: Thick and dull to thin, glistening and splashy.

patch.name: Door latch click (hollow-core)
patch.description: A cheap, light hollow-core bedroom door flicked shut on a carpeted landing: more pock than thud. 0 ms: the bolt of the small tubular latch knocks back off the strike plate, a dull bright tack. 26 ms: it springs into the keeper, the lower and louder half of the ka-chunk, a dead rattly clack with pressed-steel and plastic in it. 28 ms: the thin door skins slap the stop and the cardboard-honeycomb cavity between them answers: a boxy, hollow pock around 200 to 500 Hz, gone in 80 ms, with very little weight under it. 60 ms on: the loose skin and the handle buzz against the frame for a moment. The room is small and soft: carpet, a short dull answer.

tracks.note: Both halves of the ka-chunk from one small mechanism: a 2 ms burst of noise through a short metallic resonator with a clustered chord, so each hit is a dense clack with no clean partial. First the bolt knocking back (higher, softer), then springing home (lower, louder).
The thin door skin slapping the stop: a damped sheet of hardboard, 64 crowded modes, hit flat with something soft. The pock of the door.
The hollow inside the door answering the slap: a short burst of low noise ringing a stubby tube, the boxy colour that says the door is empty.
The loose skin and the handle chattering against the frame after the hit: a thinning burst of small dull wooden and metal ticks.

controls.label: Hollowness
controls.hint: A thin flat slap, to an empty boxy pock like knocking on the door.

controls.label: Door size
controls.hint: A cupboard or wardrobe door, to a full-height room door.

controls.label: Push
controls.hint: Clicked gently to, or flicked shut so the door slaps and the two halves of the click run together.

controls.label: Latch
controls.hint: A tiny tinny catch, to a chunkier, duller mechanism.

controls.label: Rattle
controls.hint: A snug door, or one that chatters in its frame after it lands.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry and close, a carpeted bedroom, or a bare landing.

patch.name: Heavy steel door slams
patch.description: A heavy steel security door (cell block, bunker, plant room) thrown shut in a bare concrete corridor, heard from a few metres inside. 0 to 280 ms: the slab swings in, pushing a low gust of air ahead of it, its dry hinge giving one short quiet creak. 280 ms: the door meets its steel frame: a massive, dead BOOM from the slab and the wall it hangs in, a hollow boxy bark from the door skin, and a hard, dense, crashing clang from edge on frame that the door's own mass chokes within half a second. 300 to 450 ms: loose hardware chatters in the frame. 390 ms: the spring bolt drops into its keep with a two-part ka-chunk. The corridor throws it all back: a slap off the far wall 95 ms later and two seconds of hard, bright concrete tail.

tracks.note: Air pushed ahead of the swinging slab: a low gust that swells and is cut off by the slam. No tone in it.
One short dry creak from the hinge pin just before the hit: steel dragged on steel, irregular, quiet. Turn Hinge up for a rusty door.
The mass: slab and wall taking the blow. A soft-struck, heavily damped steel box near 50 Hz whose pitch sags, driven so its weight also shows at 100 to 300 Hz on small speakers.
The hollow door skin barking: a burst of noise ringing in the box of the door (140 to 500 Hz). This is what says 'big hollow steel thing' on a laptop.
Edge on frame: a dented steel plate with 96 crowded modes, set off by a crumbling noisy contact so it crashes rather than rings, and choked by the door's mass.
Loose hardware shaken by the blow: hinge pins, the viewing flap, the bolt in its guides. A burst of small steel ticks over 160 ms.
The spring bolt: 'ka' as it rides over the strike plate, 'chunk' 48 ms later as it drops into the keep. A short fat steel lump, lower and deader than the clang.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A sheet-steel locker-room door, up to a vault slab: the boom drops, lasts longer and takes over from the clang.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: Pushed to until it meets the frame, or hurled shut: more crash, more bite on the edge, more air ahead of it.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: A gasketed door that lands with a dead thunk, or bare steel on steel that clangs on for most of a second.

controls.label: Latch
controls.hint: No lock at all, or a big bolt slamming home later and louder after the hit.

controls.label: Rattle
controls.hint: A tight, well-hung door, or one with loose pins and plates that chatter after the blow.

controls.label: Hinge
controls.hint: Greased and silent, or a dry hinge that creaks as the door swings in.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: An outside yard with nothing to answer, through a concrete corridor, to a deep stairwell that roars for seconds.

patch.name: Wooden door creak (low groan)
patch.description: A massive oak cellar door on wooden pintle hinges, leaned open very slowly: no squeal at all, only wood groaning against wood. Each slip of the hinge is a small knock that the door leaf answers with its own woody resonances (350 Hz to 2.5 kHz). The slips come one by one at first (about 9 a second, 'tok, tok, tok'), crowd together into a rattling purr (30 to 60 a second by 1.2 s) and fuse into a low, straining groan around 100 to 130 slips a second as the door passes the middle (1.6 to 2.4 s), with a catch at 2.0 s where it drops and recovers. Then it slows back through the purr to single knocks and stops at 3.1 s, the timber settling with a low thud. A second, smaller joint (the top pintle) ticks along at its own slower pace.

tracks.note: The lower hinge driving the door leaf: a modal wooden plate scraped over evenly spaced ridges, one ridge per slip, so `exciter.density` is the slip rate. Only nine modes that all ring equally long (low `damping`): few, narrow resonances are what turn a pulse train into a voiced groan instead of a zip.
The top hinge: a smaller, higher wooden joint slipping at about half the rate, never fast enough to fuse, so dry ticks ride on top of the groan and the two never line up.
The weight of the door: low thuds of the frame taking the strain at the start, at the catch, and when it comes to rest.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: Leaned open over several seconds, knock by knock, or shoved open in one short groan.

controls.label: Groan
controls.hint: Separate slow knocks that never join up, or a higher, tighter groan close to a moan.

controls.label: Dryness
controls.hint: Waxed wood that purrs evenly, or parched, gritty wood that shudders and scrapes.

controls.label: Door size
controls.hint: A small hatch with a high wooden voice, or a huge gate with a deep one and heavy thuds.

controls.label: Hollow
controls.hint: A dead, dense slab that only knocks, or a thin resonant panel that hums and sings with every slip.

controls.label: Cellar
controls.hint: Close and dry, or echoing in a stone cellar.

patch.name: Big boom with debris
patch.description: A fuel depot goes up a hundred metres away. The explosion is built the way film sound does it: a sharp, complete bang recorded 'small' (a crack, a drum-like thump and a burst of fire noise, 300 ms long) is played back at 40 % speed, so everything in it becomes slow, low and enormous: a 30 ms crack, a boom that takes most of a second to fall, and fire that roars for two. From 400 ms the debris comes down: lumps of rubble thudding and clacking, big pieces first. At 1.15 s a bent sheet of roofing steel lands with a dull crash and clatters to rest in five closing bounces.

tracks.note: The crack and fireball, before slowing: bright noise with a fast-closing filter. Varispeed turns its 0.35 s into nearly a second of roar.
The body: a drum skin struck hard, pitched like a tom, then slowed by the same factor so it lands at 60 to 150 Hz with its overtones intact.

What comes down: individual pieces of rubble, each a small dull lump of stone landing (no piece shorter than 14 ms, tops rolled off at 3.6 kHz, so they thud and clack instead of clicking), big ones first.

One large piece that lands late and clatters to rest: a bent sheet of roofing steel. A dented plate with 80 crowded, heavily damped modes, set off by a rough noisy contact spread over 8 ms, so each landing is a dull crashing 'clank' with no note; five bounces closing up, each on a different edge (pitch jitter).

controls.label: Scale
controls.hint: A car backfire-sized bang to a slow, city-shaking detonation.

controls.label: Fire
controls.hint: A dry thud, or a long roaring fireball over it.

controls.label: Debris
controls.hint: Nothing thrown, to a long rain of wreckage.

controls.label: Open air
controls.hint: Close and dry to rolling across a wide open site.

patch.name: Distant explosion in a valley
patch.description: Artillery landing four kilometres away on the far side of a mountain valley, heard from a hillside on a still evening. There is no crack: the air has taken everything above 600 Hz. What arrives is a soft, wide 'whump' of low noise, 60 to 400 Hz, felt as much as heard, with a second, weaker arrival 170 ms behind it by another path (the 'ka-rump' of far guns). Then the valley plays with it: an echo off the near slope 650 ms later, another off the far wall at 1.3 s, each darker and softer, over a low ground roll that heaves and wanders and takes five seconds to die.

tracks.note: The blast as it arrives: a soft-edged burst of brown noise whose lowpass closes from 680 to 180 Hz, then a weaker second arrival. Noise, so it is a pressure 'whump' and not a drum note; tube drive and a 260 Hz lift keep it alive on small speakers.
The weight under the whump: a very large slack skin set off by a 60 ms push of noise, sagging in pitch and gone in 0.4 s. Kept well under the noise so no note hangs in the valley.
The rumble that follows along the ground: brown noise, slowly heaving (random tremolo, wander on the cutoff), mostly under 350 Hz.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: A kilometre off, with a knock and some grit left in it, to far beyond the ridge: only a slow soft pressure.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A mortar round's short bump to a magazine going up: lower, longer, with more ground roll.

controls.label: Echoes
controls.hint: Flat open plain, one thump, to a deep valley that answers again and again.

controls.label: Valley width
controls.hint: A narrow gorge with quick echoes to a wide basin with slow ones.

controls.label: Rumble
controls.hint: Just the thump and its echoes, or a long ground-rolling rumble after it.

patch.name: Firework rocket
patch.description: A rocket at a town display, watched from the square. 0 ms: the fuse lights and it leaves the tube with a short fizzing 'fsst'. 0 to 1.1 s: it climbs, screaming: a whistle (noise in a narrow pipe) that rises from 1.4 to 3.3 kHz with a fast warble and thins as it gets higher and farther. 1.1 to 1.3 s: silence. 1.3 s: the shell bursts 150 m up: a broad, unpitched 'BOOM' of noise that opens bright and closes dark in a third of a second, with a short hollow thump under it, already rounded by the distance. Then the stars: two seconds of thick crackling as they burn out, drifting down, while the bang comes back off the buildings.

tracks.note: Lift-off: a fizz of violet noise and a small hollow thump from the mortar tube.
The screamer: noise forced through a tube resonator that climbs. The 26 Hz warble is the whistle composition burning unevenly; the gain curve is the rocket getting farther away.

The shell breaking, the main event: a burst of white noise whose lowpass falls from 7 kHz to 220 Hz in 0.3 s, saturated. Broadband, so it is a bang and not a drum; the 'height' lowpass is 150 m of air.
The thump under the bang: a slack membrane pushed by 80 ms of noise, damped so it sags and is gone in 0.3 s. Weight only; it must not ring as a note.
The stars burning out, the signature of a firework: crackle that stays thick for most of a second after the burst and then thins, spread across the sky.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: A low garden rocket, bursting soon and bright, to a big shell high up: a longer climb and a duller, later boom.

controls.label: Shell size
controls.hint: A small pop of colour to a chest-thumping aerial shell.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: A silent climb, or a loud screaming one.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: A plain burst, or a long glittering crackle of stars.

controls.label: Town
controls.hint: Open field to a square ringed with buildings throwing the bang back.

patch.name: Grenade
patch.description: A fragmentation grenade bursting in soft earth twenty metres off, in open country with a treeline. 0 ms: the detonation, a hard clipped crack with no pitch at all. 2 ms: the blast body, a burst of dark noise that closes from 5 kHz to 150 Hz in a fifth of a second (a 'KRAK-whump', not a note), and the ground taking the blow as a dead, crowded thud. 20 to 500 ms: a fountain of soil hisses up and out. 60 to 500 ms: steel splinters whip past and clack off stones. 180 ms to 1.2 s: clods and soil thud back down, thinning out. 350 ms: the treeline hands the bang back, dull, and rolls for a second.

tracks.note: Detonation: a few ms of hard-clipped white noise. High explosive is a shock, not a boom: this sets the scale and is the loudest instant.
The pressure wave: pink noise through a fast-closing, wandering lowpass, saturated so it is a thick ragged 'whump' 80 to 600 Hz wide. Noise, so it has weight but no note.
The earth taking the blow: a huge damped slab (96 crowded modes, the lowest filtered away) reached over 12 ms, so it is a dead pitchless thud at 90 to 400 Hz under the blast.
The fountain of soil going up: thousands of tiny grit ticks, densest at once and gone in half a second. A dry 'pshh' that makes it earth and not a drum.
Steel splinters hitting stones and trunks: short dead clacks and ticks, no ring. Scattered through the first half second.
Two or three splinters whipping past the listener: short falling zips, quiet. Follows the Shrapnel control.
Clods and soil raining back: dull little lumps (stone grains kept low and short, lowpassed), big ones first, for a second.

controls.label: Charge
controls.hint: A flash-bang's short bark to a satchel charge: darker, longer, heavier, more ground in it.

controls.label: Punch
controls.hint: A soft whump to a chest-hitting slam with a hard crack on the front.

controls.label: Shrapnel
controls.hint: A plain blast, or steel splinters zipping past and clacking off everything.

controls.label: Dirt
controls.hint: Hard ground, nothing thrown, to a fountain of soil hissing up and thudding back down for two seconds.

controls.label: Roll
controls.hint: Flat and dry, or echoing back off a far treeline and rolling.

patch.name: Firecracker pop
patch.description: A single firecracker going off on a pavement three metres away. 0 ms: the bang, a hard unpitched crack of full-band noise that darkens within 60 ms as the paper tube bursts, with a short low thump of pushed air under it. 1 ms: the tube itself, a dead hollow cardboard colour on the bang, gone in 40 ms, never a note. 15 to 300 ms: shreds of paper and grit patter down on the pavement. 55 ms: one hard echo off the house across the street, duller, then a short street tail.

tracks.note: The bang: clipped white noise, full-band for the first few ms and closing to 1 kHz by 60 ms. Unpitched; this is the firecracker.
The push of air: a 50 ms burst of pink noise under 500 Hz. Gives the bang weight at 120 to 450 Hz without a pitch.
The paper tube bursting: a dented cardboard pipe with 40 crowded modes, heavily damped, set off by 20 ms of rough noise. A hollow colour on the bang that says 'small and paper', not a 'pok'.
Paper and grit landing: sparse dry ticks, thinning out.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A toy cap, a tiny snap, to a fat banger with a hollow thump.

controls.label: Snap
controls.hint: A dull damp pop to an ear-stinging crack.

controls.label: Shreds
controls.hint: Paper and grit raining down afterwards.

controls.label: Street
controls.hint: Open field, no echo, to a narrow alley slapping it back.

patch.name: Footstep: leather shoe on concrete
patch.description: One step of a hard-soled leather shoe on a polished concrete corridor floor. 0 ms: the stacked leather heel lands with a short, hard, dry knock (a crowd of damped modes with a 3 ms click on its leading edge, not a note) and the slab answers with a dead low thud; 95 ms later the sole rolls down with a softer, duller pat and a faint scuff of grit under it, and the slab thuds again, smaller; the corridor gives each a short dark slap. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: Heel strike: the stacked leather heel block, small, hard and well damped: many crowded modes that die in 25 ms, so it knocks and does not ring.
The hard edge of the heel meeting concrete: 3 ms of bright noise, the 'tick' of a dress shoe.
The floor answering: a concrete slab is a huge plate, so a dead crowd of modes at 100 to 400 Hz gives the step its weight without a note. Again, smaller, under the sole.
The sole rolling down 95 ms after the heel: leather pat and a little grit scuff.

controls.label: Shoe
controls.hint: A soft sneaker that pads, to a dress shoe, to a hard stiletto click.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light quick step to a heavy stomp.

controls.label: Pace
controls.hint: A slow stroll with the heel and sole far apart, to a run where they land together.

controls.label: Scuff
controls.hint: A clean placed step, or a dragged sole on a gritty floor.

controls.label: Corridor
controls.hint: Dry, or a long empty corridor.

patch.name: Footstep: creaky wooden floor
patch.description: One slow step on an old floorboard in a quiet house at night. 0 ms: a socked heel lands with a low hollow knock, the boards and the space under them answering as a dull crowd of low modes with no note; from 50 ms, as the weight comes on, the board rubs on its nail: a stick-slip creak of about 370 ms that starts as a few separate ticks, fuses into a nasal groan climbing to about 230 slips a second, wavers, sags and breaks back into single ticks as it stops. The board is the loudspeaker: its fixed resonances (520 Hz to 3.3 kHz) give the gliding slip rate a small wooden voice. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: The step: a soft heel on a boarded floor over a hollow. A big wooden panel, so a crowd of modes at 100 to 400 Hz and no single pitch.
The foot itself: the small dull pat of a sock or the knock of a hard sole, a few ms of noise before the floor answers.

The board rubbing on its nail under the weight: stick-slip pulses (a voice source used as a friction oscillator, one sharp pulse per slip) through the board's fixed resonances. `freq` is the slip rate, so it is the story: ticks, groan, waver, sag, ticks.

controls.label: Creak
controls.hint: A sound board that only thumps, a short complaint, or a long loud groan as the weight comes on slowly.

controls.label: Board
controls.hint: A thick old beam that groans low, to a thin dry board that squeaks.

controls.label: Dry
controls.hint: A smooth, almost sung creak, or a dry cracked board that stutters and rasps.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A cat-light step to a heavy man: a louder, lower, longer knock from the floor.

controls.label: Shoe
controls.hint: Bare feet and socks, or hard boots that knock.

controls.label: House
controls.hint: Close and dry, or an empty room.

patch.name: Footstep: gravel
patch.description: One step of a walking boot on a loose gravel drive, outdoors. 0 ms: the heel digs in and a hundred pea-sized stones grind and click against each other, thick for the first 50 ms and thinning over 110 ms; from 60 ms, before the heel has finished, the ball of the foot rolls forward with a second, longer and finer crunch as stones are pushed away (to about 300 ms); under both runs the continuous gritty grind of the boot sinking in, and a dull, dead thump of the packed ground under the heel gives the step its body. No echo: open air. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: Heel crunch: a thick run of small stones knocking together, coarse and loud, thinning as the heel beds in.
Toe roll: a longer, finer, quieter crunch as the foot pushes off, overlapping the heel so the step is one event.
The boot sinking in: the continuous gritty rub of stones sliding under the sole, flickering, which fills the gaps between the separate clicks.
The packed earth under the stones: a dull, dead thump (a crowd of low modes, no note) so the step has a body.

controls.label: Stones
controls.hint: Fine grit and sand to coarse river pebbles that clack.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A child tiptoeing to a soldier with a pack.

controls.label: Pace
controls.hint: A slow careful step with a long toe roll, to a run that lands all at once.

controls.label: Wet
controls.hint: Dry dusty gravel, crisp and bright, or rain-soaked and dull.

patch.name: Footstep: metal grate
patch.description: One step of a work boot on a steel catwalk grating in a ship's engine room. 0 ms: the rubber sole lands with a dull thud and the heavy panel clanks: a dense, sour, low clang of many crowded bars (150 Hz to 1 kHz, no one note) that dies in a third of a second; the loose panel chatters down onto its frame clips, four quick dull steel knocks closing up from 35 ms apart, with a sprinkle of small metallic ticks from the bars; the steel compartment rings back, short and hard.

tracks.note: The grating: a heavy welded lattice struck by a rubber sole. A big panel, so the modes are low, crowded and dented: a clank, not a ting.
The loose panel chattering on its frame clips: a small, dead steel knock repeated four times, closing up and dying.
The bars of the lattice ticking against each other after the blow: a short sprinkle of small, dead steel ticks.
The boot itself: a soft rubber thud under the clang.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light quick step to a heavy armoured stomp.

controls.label: Loose
controls.hint: A welded deck that only rings, or a loose panel that clatters on its frame.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Thick damped plate that clunks, to thin grating that sings.

controls.label: Panel
controls.hint: A small stair tread to a long span of walkway.

controls.label: Compartment
controls.hint: Open air gantry, or deep inside a steel hull.

patch.name: Footstep: puddle splash
patch.description: One step of a rubber boot into a shallow street puddle. 0 ms: the sole slaps the water with a flat, wet, broadband smack that takes 160 ms to close down; under it the boot meets the asphalt with a dull thud and the water closing round the boot gives a short hollow gurgle (noise in a small cavity, rising, no clear note); the water thrown out sideways hisses through the air and lands as spray from 20 to 330 ms, a flickering wash of noise with a fine patter of droplets on top, getting thinner and higher as it dies. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: Sole on water: a flat burst of noise that closes down over 160 ms, like a hand slapping a bath. The body of the sound.
The sheet of water thrown out and coming down: hissing, flickering noise that rises and thins as the drops get smaller.
The spray landing back on the puddle: a dense patter of very short droplets, too many and too brief to hear as notes.
Water closing round the boot: dark noise in a small hollow that tightens as it fills, a gurgle and not a bloop.
The street under the water: a dead thud, a crowd of low modes.

controls.label: Depth
controls.hint: A wet pavement to an ankle-deep puddle: more hollow gurgle, lower and longer, and less street under it.

controls.label: Splash
controls.hint: A careful step, or a jump that throws water everywhere.

controls.label: Stomp
controls.hint: A soft wade in, or a hard flat slap.

controls.label: Street
controls.hint: Open and dry-sounding, or between wet walls.

patch.name: Footstep: snow
patch.description: One step in ankle-deep cold snow on a still winter day. No impact at all: the boot presses down over 180 ms and the snow compacts with a creaking, squeaking crunch that swells as the weight comes on and stops when the foot is down; under it a soft muffled whumpf; then 60 ms of fine crystals falling back into the print. Close, dead, no echo: snow swallows everything. Use the variations for a walk.

tracks.note: Snow compacting: crackling noise through a narrow resonance that slides down as the snow packs. The creak of cold snow.
The crust and grains breaking under the sole: many small dull ticks, thickest in the middle of the step.
The weight going into the snow pack: a soft low push, no attack.
Loose crystals falling back into the footprint after the step.

controls.label: Cold
controls.hint: Wet slushy snow that squelches dully, to dry powder at -20 that squeaks.

controls.label: Depth
controls.hint: A dusting over hard ground, or knee-deep drifts: a longer, lower press.

controls.label: Crust
controls.hint: Soft fresh snow, or an icy crust that cracks under the boot.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light step to a heavy one that sinks.

patch.name: Body punch
patch.description: A film-style punch to the ribs, miked close. -45 ms: the sleeve cuts the air, a short swish rising in pitch; 0 ms: the fist sinks in over about 10 ms, a wet leathery smack on top of a dead, crowded thump of flesh and a chesty 'oof' of displaced body (150 to 400 Hz, no note, sagging as the chest gives), with a dull cracked knuckle-on-rib knock inside it; all of it is over in 150 ms, squeezed hard like a movie fight.

tracks.note: The arm coming: 45 ms of sleeve and air before the hit, cut off by it.
The thump: a soft dead mass the fist sinks into over 10 ms. Forty crowded, dented modes that die at once, so it is a thud, not a drum; the pitch sags as the body gives.
The weight a laptop can play: the chest cavity giving, a burst of dark noise closing from 900 to 220 Hz in 60 ms.
Skin and cloth: the wet slap on top, the part laptop speakers carry.
Knuckles on ribs: a short, cracked woody knock inside the thump.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A jab to a heavyweight body blow: lower, fatter, a little longer.

controls.label: Smack
controls.hint: A muffled hit through a coat, or a bare wet slap.

controls.label: Bone
controls.hint: All soft tissue, or a crack of knuckle on rib.

controls.label: Swing
controls.hint: A short jab with barely a rustle of sleeve before it, or a long telegraphed swing you hear coming.

patch.name: Cardboard box dropped
patch.description: A half-full moving box dropped from knee height onto a laminate floor. 0 ms: it lands on one bottom edge with a dead papery whump; at 95 ms it tips flat with a second, softer and lower thump; from 20 ms the things inside (books, loose cutlery) slide and knock against the walls for a third of a second. No ring anywhere: cardboard eats it.

tracks.note: The box: a dead cardboard cavity. Two events: the edge lands, then it tips flat.
The flat face slapping the floor: papery mid noise, on the second landing.
What is inside, sliding and knocking the walls.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A shoebox to a wardrobe carton.

controls.label: Contents
controls.hint: Empty, or packed with things that slide and knock.

controls.label: Hard stuff
controls.hint: Soft clothes and books inside, or cutlery and tins.

controls.label: Drop
controls.hint: Set down gently to dropped from the shoulder: harder, with a livelier tumble.

patch.name: Coin dropped and settling
patch.description: A large coin dropped a hand-width onto a wooden table top. 0 ms: it lands on its edge with a bright ring; it hops four or five times, faster and faster and a little wild because it is spinning; near 600 ms it falls onto its face and wobbles round its rim, the rattle speeding up and rising in pitch as it flattens, until it stops dead at about 1.4 s. The table knocks softly under the first hits.

tracks.note: The coin bouncing on its edge: one small metal disc, each hop sooner and softer.
The spin-down: the coin rolling round its rim, faster and higher until it lies flat.
The table top under the first hits: a soft wooden knock that gives it a place.

controls.label: Coin
controls.hint: A tiny thin coin that tinks to a heavy silver dollar.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: Slipped from the fingers, or dropped from standing: longer hops.

controls.label: Spin
controls.hint: Lands flat and stops, or spins down in a long rising rattle.

controls.label: Table
controls.hint: Stone counter with no voice, or a hollow wooden table that knocks.

patch.name: Knock on a wooden door
patch.description: Knuckles on a panelled interior door, heard from the hallway side: three raps about 170 ms apart, a hand's rhythm, the first the firmest and each one a touch later and softer. Each rap is a bony knuckle click, then the whole door leaf answering with a dense, dry, pitchless knock (its crowd of modes at 120 to 450 Hz) and the hollow of the panel giving a short boxy cough; the room behind the door returns a short muffled bloom.

tracks.note: The door leaf: a big wooden plate whose lowest modes are too low to hear, so the knock is the crowd above them, damped and dented, with no note. High-passed because a door barely radiates below 100 Hz. The envelope only fades the inaudible low modes out before the voice ends.
The hollow of the panel: a 25 ms puff of noise coughing in a shallow box near 210 Hz. This is what says 'door' and not 'table'.
Bone on wood: the small hard, slightly cracked click on top of each rap.

controls.label: Knocks
controls.hint: One rap to five.

controls.label: Urgency
controls.hint: A slow polite tap to fast hard pounding.

controls.label: Door
controls.hint: A thin hollow-core door that barks and booms, to a thick oak one that gives a short dead knock.

controls.label: Room behind
controls.hint: Nothing behind the door, or an empty room that answers.

patch.name: Giant metal slam
patch.description: A blast door the size of a house dropping shut in an empty hangar, heard from well back. 0 to 300 ms: the slab falls the last metre in its guides, steel shrieking low on steel, air rushing out from under it. 300 ms: thousands of tons of plate meet the sill, not a clang but a crumbling, crowded CRASH, with the concrete floor taking the blow as a dead pitchless boom. 440 and 640 ms: the slab bounces and settles, two smaller, lower landings. For a second after, the plate groans as it grinds to rest in its frame and shaken-loose bolts and scale rain onto the floor. The hangar answers 70 ms behind with a long dark roar whose low end clears first.

tracks.note: The last metre of the drop: the slab dragging down its guides, a low ragged steel shriek that speeds up, plus nothing tonal. Cut off by the landing.
Air squeezed out from under the falling slab: a dark gust that swells into the hit.

The door meeting the sill: a huge dented steel plate, 96 crowded modes, landing along its whole edge over 15 ms and set off by crumbling noise, so it crashes instead of tolling. Two smaller landings follow as it bounces and settles.
The weight: the concrete floor slab taking the blow, a soft wide landing on a crowd of dead low modes (60 to 300 Hz, no note), driven so small speakers show it.
The crumbling part of the crash: scale, sill and sheet steel breaking up, a noise burst that darkens from 3 kHz to 350 Hz in half a second.
The slab grinding to rest in its frame: a big steel plate dragged over grit, the drag slowing from 40 to 11 catches a second, its pitch sagging.
Bolts, scale and rust shaken loose, hitting the floor for a second: big dull steel lumps first, grit after.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A shipping container door to a dam gate: lower, longer, more floor in it.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Standing under it, or hearing it from the far end of the hall: more roar, less edge.

controls.label: Debris
controls.hint: A clean close, or bolts and rust raining after it.

controls.label: Rust
controls.hint: New machined steel that lands with a long clang, or a corroded wreck that shrieks down, crunches and grinds.

controls.label: Hall
controls.hint: A big workshop to an endless cavern.

patch.name: Two glasses clink
patch.description: Two wine glasses touched rim to rim in a toast, close to the ear at a dinner table. The two bowls are slightly different sizes, so two clear notes a wide third apart ring together; the second glass speaks 3 ms after the first; each is not quite round, so its note shimmers; the wine inside dulls the top of the ring.

tracks.note: Your glass: the lower note.
Their glass: a little smaller and thinner, 3 ms late.
The contact itself: a dry glassy tick.

controls.label: Glass size
controls.hint: Shot glasses that tink to big balloon glasses that sing low.

controls.label: Fill
controls.hint: Empty crystal that rings on, or full glasses whose ring is short and dull.

controls.label: Toast
controls.hint: A careful touch to an enthusiastic clack.

controls.label: Mismatch
controls.hint: A matched pair on one note, or two odd glasses far apart.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry at the ear, or across a dining room.

patch.name: Glass shatters
patch.description: A window pane broken by a thrown stone, heard from inside a kitchen. 0 ms: the stone knocks the pane in its wooden frame and the glass gives way with one hard, noisy crash, a bright wash of breaking that lasts about 120 ms; from 10 ms the pieces let go, thousands in the first tenth of a second, thinning within half a second to dry single ticks and clinks, the big pieces low and loud, the splinters high and faint, none of them ringing long enough to be a note; from 250 ms a few larger shards hit the tiled floor and chatter to rest, each one bouncing faster and fainter.

tracks.note: The pane giving way: a sheet of glass excited by a rough, crumbling hit.
The break itself: a wash of bright noise for the first 120 ms, the thousand cracks no one can count.
The stone meeting the pane in its wooden frame: the low knock that gives the break a body.
The pieces: a dense spray of small dead glass ticks and clinks, front-loaded, thinning to single dry tinkles. Short rings so no piece is a note.
Larger shards landing on the tiles: four pieces, each bouncing to rest in a quickening chatter of dry clinks.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A drinking glass to a shop window: lower, longer, the pieces falling for longer.

controls.label: Pieces
controls.hint: A clean break into a few big pieces, or an explosion of splinters.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Carpet that swallows the pieces, or hard tiles they dance on.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: A crack that lets go slowly, or a violent smash.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dry, or a hard tiled room.

patch.name: Metal pipe struck
patch.description: A length of steel scaffolding pipe hanging from one hand, struck near its end with a wrench in a concrete garage. 0 ms: the steel-on-steel tick; from 2 ms the pipe rings on its bar modes, slightly out of round so every partial beats slowly; under it the air inside the pipe answers with a short hollow bonk; the garage returns a hard slap.

tracks.note: The pipe itself: a free steel bar hit near the end, slightly bent so the partials beat.
The air column inside: a wrench tick ringing a hollow tube, the "bonk" that says pipe and not rod.
The first 3 ms of steel on steel.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A short offcut that pings to a long heavy pole that tolls.

controls.label: Strike
controls.hint: A rubber boot heel to a steel wrench: duller and rounder, or brighter with a hard tick.

controls.label: Grip
controls.hint: Hanging free and singing, or clamped in a fist so the ring chokes at once.

controls.label: Hollow
controls.hint: A solid bar, or a wide pipe whose air column bonks.

controls.label: Garage
controls.hint: Dry and close, or ringing off the concrete walls.

patch.name: Rock on rock
patch.description: A fist-sized river stone thrown down onto a boulder in a dry gorge. 0 ms: a hard, bright, pitchless CRACK, the small stone's click and a splintering snap of grit on top, with only a dull dead thud from the boulder under it; 60 and 100 ms: the stone hops twice and comes to rest, two quick lighter clacks; from 6 ms chips and grit skitter off for a third of a second; about 175 ms after the hit the far wall of the gorge sends the crack back once, darker, with a ghost of a second return, and the rock around it gives a short dark wash.

tracks.note: The thrown stone: a small, flawed, irregular lump hit hard. Its click at 1.5 to 5 kHz is the sound; two lighter hops follow as it settles.
The snap of the contact itself: 4 ms of bright noise, grit crushed between the two faces.
The boulder: far too massive to answer with a note, so only a dull, dead, spread thud at 200 to 600 Hz, 1 ms behind and well under the stone.
Chips and grit skipping away after the hit, for a third of a second.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: Two pebbles clicking to a rock the size of a head landing: lower, longer, more thud.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: A tap to a hard throw that snaps and knocks chips off.

controls.label: Stone
controls.hint: Soft crumbly sandstone that thuds, to glassy flint that clicks and rings a moment.

controls.label: Gorge
controls.hint: Open ground with no echo, or rock walls that throw the crack back.

controls.label: Wall distance
controls.hint: A wall 15 metres off to one 100 metres away: a later echo.

patch.name: Rubber ball bounces to rest
patch.description: A solid rubber bouncy ball dropped from waist height onto a wooden gym floor. First bounce at 0 ms, the next about 310 ms later, each gap about four fifths of the last, each hit softer, until the bounces run together into a short buzz and stop near 2 s. Every bounce is the same ball: a round, pitched "pock" with the hollow floor answering under it, in a big empty gym.

tracks.note: The ball: one rubber sphere bouncing, each gap a fixed fraction of the last.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: Dropped from a hand-width, or thrown down from overhead: longer gaps, more bounces.

controls.label: Bounciness
controls.hint: A dead ball that stops in three hops, or a super ball that will not quit.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A marble-sized super ball to a basketball.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Solid concrete, or a hollow wooden floor that booms with each bounce.

controls.label: Gym
controls.hint: A small room to an empty sports hall.

patch.name: Heavy sack thud
patch.description: A 25 kg sack of grain dropped off a shoulder onto the plank floor of a barn. 0 ms: a soft, wide whump with no click at all, the burlap spreading for 40 ms rather than hitting; the floor planks boom once underneath around 100 Hz and its neighbours; from 30 ms the grain inside slumps with a short dry hiss; a little dust and a wooden room around it.

tracks.note: The sack landing: dark noise that opens and closes in 60 ms. A spread, not a hit.
The planks: a big wooden cavity kicked by something soft, the pitch of the thud.
The contents slumping after the landing: a dry hiss of small grains.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A pillow to a body: lower, longer, more floor.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Packed earth that gives nothing back, or a hollow stage that booms.

controls.label: Filling
controls.hint: A solid lump, or loose grain that hisses as it settles.

controls.label: Slap
controls.hint: A soft slump, or a flat landing with a leathery slap.

controls.label: Barn
controls.hint: Dry and close, or in a big wooden room.

patch.name: Trash can kicked
patch.description: A dented galvanised trash can kicked hard in a back alley. 0 ms: the boot lands on the thin steel wall with a dull bong (rubber sole, so no tick); the wall is creased, so the clang is sour and uneven and buckles downward in pitch for the first 60 ms; from 30 ms the loose lid chatters on the rim for half a second, slowing down; brick walls throw back a short hard echo.

tracks.note: The can wall: thin dented sheet steel hit by a soft boot. The pitch sag is the sheet buckling.
The loose lid rattling on the rim: a rolling chatter that slows to a stop.
The empty drum: the low breath of the can body under the clang.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A paint tin to an oil drum.

controls.label: Kick
controls.hint: A nudge with a sneaker to a full swing with a steel toecap.

controls.label: Dents
controls.hint: A new can with a clean clang to battered junk.

controls.label: Lid
controls.hint: No lid, or a loose one that chatters on.

controls.label: Alley
controls.hint: Open yard to a narrow brick alley.

patch.name: Dark curse
patch.description: A curse is laid in a crypt. 0 to 800 ms: a whisper that is sucked backwards into the caster's mouth (breathy syllables recorded forwards, played in reverse, so each one swells and stops dead). 800 ms: the curse lands. A huge throat, something far bigger than a person, lets out a falling growl from 'ah' down to a closed 'oo', its pitch sinking a fifth over 1.2 s, ring-modulated at 41 Hz so it rattles. A tenth of a second later a cracked iron bell tolls once over it, a little flat, its clang sitting above the growl. The crypt keeps both for three seconds.

tracks.note: The incantation, reversed: four whispered syllables (voice with no tone, only breath), each with its own vowel sweep. The reverse makes them inhale.
What answers: a giant throat growling down. Growl adds the octave-below snarl; the ring modulator makes it shake like something not alive.

The toll that marks it: a big cracked bell (dent), its modes beating slowly. Its strike lands 100 ms after the growl starts and its partials sit at 400 Hz to 2 kHz, above the throat, so it is heard as its own event.

controls.label: Menace
controls.hint: A petty hex to something enormous and very angry.

controls.label: Whisper
controls.hint: No incantation, or loud hissing syllables before it lands.

controls.label: Rattle
controls.hint: A living throat to a shuddering, undead buzz.

controls.label: Bell
controls.hint: No toll, or a great cracked bell over the growl.

controls.label: Crypt
controls.hint: Close in a small cell, or lost in a vast vault.

patch.name: Fireball
patch.description: A fireball lit in the caster's hand and thrown. 0 ms: ignition, a soft 'whoomp' as the air catches (low noise opening quickly from 150 Hz to 2 kHz, with a pressure thump under it). 0 to 1.3 s: the ball roars and flutters like a torch swung through the air, and it travels away from you, so the roar drops in pitch, dulls and fades. All the way it spits and crackles: bright embers popping off and a few fat, low spits of resin, thinning as it goes.

tracks.note: Ignition: the pressure thump. A big soft membrane, not a sine drop, so it sounds like air and not a kick drum.
The flame: pink noise whose filter flutters at random (wander plus a fast random tremolo) is what makes it burn instead of hiss. Doppler carries it away.
Sparks and pops: sharp, uneven, never regular. Without them it is wind.
The fat in the fire: a few low, loud pops and spits of resin, scattered along the flight. They are what a listener calls 'fire'.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A candle-sized firebolt to a cart-sized ball of flame.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: Smooth clean flame to a spitting, popping blaze.

controls.label: Flutter
controls.hint: A steady jet to a wildly guttering torch.

controls.label: Throw
controls.hint: Held burning in the hand, or hurled away fast.

controls.label: Ignition
controls.hint: How hard it catches at the start.

patch.name: Healing spell
patch.description: A healer lays hands on a wound in a stone chapel. A small choir of soft voices breathes in on 'oo' and opens to 'ah' over 1.2 s, rising a tone as the light comes. Across it a harp runs upward, eight nylon strings plucked by a thumb in 600 ms. The warmth stays for a moment in the chapel and fades. Nothing sharp anywhere: it should feel like breathing out.

tracks.note: The warmth: real throats (voice model), soft tension, lots of breath. Chorus makes three singers of one.
A second, lower part a fifth below: body for small speakers, and it makes the choir a chord.
The gesture: a rising run, soft thumb plucks, slowing slightly toward the top.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A quick potion sip to a long, slow restoration.

controls.label: Voices
controls.hint: Children's choir, high and small, down to monks.

controls.label: Breath
controls.hint: Clear sung tone to an airy whispered sigh.

controls.label: Harp
controls.hint: Voices alone, or a bright run of strings across them.

controls.label: Chapel
controls.hint: A small quiet room to a tall stone nave.

patch.name: Ice spell crack
patch.description: A frost spell freezes a puddle solid and the ice splits. 0 to 550 ms: frost racing across the surface, a dry, tight squeak-scrape over a thin glassy sheet that rises in pitch as it closes in, with crystals crackling faster and faster on top. 560 ms: the sheet cracks, a hard, bright, short snap (a brittle ceramic-like plate, badly flawed), with a second smaller crack 70 ms later as the fracture runs. Then splinters skitter away on the ice for half a second, and a cold thin breath of air hangs over it.

tracks.note: Freezing: a scrape exciter on a glass plate. The ridges come fast from the start (150 a second, so a squeak and never a ratchet) and the rate climbs, so the squeak tightens. High damping keeps it dry: ice, not a wine glass.
Crystals forming: tiny bright pops, a few at first and then a rush of them as the freeze closes. The fine crackle that says ice and not a squeaky hinge.
The split: the loudest, shortest thing. A flawed ceramic plate hit at its edge with steel; the transient shaper makes it snap. Two events: the crack, and the fracture running on.
The thickness of the ice giving way under the crack: a dull stone knock at 170 Hz so the snap has weight on small speakers.
Shards skittering off across the ice after the crack: small glass pieces, big ones first.
Cold air: a thin high hiss that swells with the freeze and lingers. Makes the space feel frozen.

controls.label: Freeze time
controls.hint: An instant flash-freeze to a long creeping frost before the crack.

controls.label: Thickness
controls.hint: A thin brittle skin of ice to a thick slab that booms when it splits.

controls.label: Crack
controls.hint: A soft tick to a vicious snap.

controls.label: Splinters
controls.hint: A clean split, or shards scattering everywhere.

controls.label: Cold air
controls.hint: The thin frozen hiss over everything.

patch.name: Portal opening
patch.description: A doorway to somewhere else is forced open in a cave. It opens like a mouth: a deep buzzing drone (two sines grinding against each other) is shaped by a giant throat that moves from a closed 'oo' to a wide 'ah' over 1.8 s, growing as it goes. The rim spins: a rotor-like chop that starts at 3 beats a second and accelerates to 14 as the portal stabilises. Wind from the other side whistles through the gap, rising. At 1.8 s it arrives: the gate locks open with a heavy stone thud that the whole cave answers, the drone at its loudest and widest. It holds open for a moment and then sinks back into the cave's long echo.

tracks.note: The portal's voice: cross-modulated sines for a thick, unstable buzz, then a formant filter with a huge throat. The vowel opening is the door opening.
Air from the other side: noise whistling through a tube whose note climbs as the gap widens. Wander keeps it gusting.
The edge burning: glittering metal shimmer from sparse crackles ringing a metal resonator. High and wide, chopped by the same spin as the drone, so the chop is heard as a turning edge.

The arrival: the gate locking open. A slab of rock taking the load all at once (a big stone plate, its blow spread over 12 ms), a crowded knock at 100 to 400 Hz with no note of its own, thrown into the cave.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A keyhole rift to a gate a dragon could walk through.

controls.label: Opening time
controls.hint: Ripped open in a moment, or slowly prised apart.

controls.label: Spin
controls.hint: A still doorway to a hard-chopping vortex.

controls.label: Menace
controls.hint: A calm humming gate to a grinding, tearing wound in the air.

controls.label: Wind
controls.hint: How much air howls through from the other side.

patch.name: Sparkle pickup
patch.description: The hero's hand closes on a floating star shard. Five tiny glass notes run up a pentatonic scale in 240 ms, each one a small bowl-shaped chime with its partials beating, the top one struck a little harder and left to ring half as long again. As they rise, a puff of fairy dust goes up with them: separate pure pings from 5 to 14 kHz, above the notes, that climb and thin out over most of a second and are still glittering after the last note. All of it in a bright plate so it glows instead of clicking.

tracks.note: The melody: glass-bowl ratios (1, 2.32, 4.25, 6.63), not a synth beep. Slightly uneven timing and velocities so a hand could have played it.
The last note, an octave up: the same glass, left to ring half as long again so the run arrives somewhere.
Fairy dust: separate pings, their range rising. This is what makes it magic and not a coin.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big warm gem to a tiny glittering shard.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Short muted ticks to long singing glass.

controls.label: Dust
controls.hint: Just the notes, or a whole cloud of glitter around them.

controls.label: Glow
controls.hint: Dry and close, or hanging in the air.

patch.name: Spell cast
patch.description: A mage throws an arcane bolt. 0 to 420 ms: energy is drawn into the staff, an unstable tone that wanders and climbs (an attractor being wound tighter), ringing a chord of sympathetic strings as it goes. Just before 420 ms it holds its breath for 30 ms. 420 ms: release. The staff head clangs, short, with strange overtones, and the bolt leaves: a tear of air as loud as the clang that sweeps up, drops in pitch and dulls as it flies away from you. Behind it a trail of rising sparks for most of a second, and the string chord left hanging in a stone hall.

tracks.note: Drawing power: a Lorenz attractor, sped up and made less stable. The string resonator turns its buzz into a chord, so the wind-up is musical. It cuts out for 30 ms before the release, so the cast hits out of a gap.

The cast itself: a short FM clang with inharmonic ratios whose brightness dies faster than its level, gone in 0.6 s so the tail belongs to the bolt, the sparks and the strings. Pitch kicks upward at the start, like something leaving.

The bolt leaving: air torn open, as loud as the clang for its first 100 ms, then carried away from you by the doppler (falling, dulling, fading). Starts 20 ms before the bell so the release has a leading edge. Without it the spell is only struck, never thrown.
What is left in the air: sparks that chirp upward, scattered along the bolt's path for most of a second.

controls.label: Charge time
controls.hint: An instant snap cast to a long, wound-up incantation.

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: A cantrip, small and high, to a heavy, clanging great spell.

controls.label: Wildness
controls.hint: Disciplined, tonal magic to raw crackling chaos.

controls.label: Whoosh
controls.hint: How much air the bolt tears on its way out.

controls.label: Hall
controls.hint: Outdoors and dry, or echoing in a stone chamber.

patch.name: Chain rattle
patch.description: Two metres of steel chain hauled off a hook and dropped in a heap on a concrete floor. 0 to 500 ms: the chain is dragged, links clinking against each other in a busy uneven patter, a few big links clanking low; around 550 ms the run thickens into a rush as it slides off; by 1 s the pile lands and the last links trickle down and settle with a few separate clinks. A bare concrete room.

tracks.note: The links hitting each other: many small steel rings, busy then a rush then a trickle.
The weight of it: slack loops and big links clanking low, fewer and louder.
The heap landing on concrete: a gritty low scrape under the rush.

controls.label: Gauge
controls.hint: A fine necklace chain that tinkles to ship's anchor chain that clanks.

controls.label: Busy
controls.hint: A lazy sway with single clinks, to a frantic shake.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A short jerk on the chain, or a long haul.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: Held in the air, or dragged and dumped on concrete.

controls.label: Cell
controls.hint: Dry, or a bare stone cell.

patch.name: Clock ticking (loop)
patch.description: A wooden mantel clock on a shelf in a quiet room, looping one second: tick at 0 ms, tock at 500 ms. Each beat is the escape wheel tooth dropping on a pallet, a tiny bright steel click, with a second fainter click 9 ms later as the pallet locks, and the clock's wooden case turning it into a soft hollow knock. The tock is a shade lower and duller than the tick, and the pair is not quite even, as in a clock slightly out of beat.

tracks.note: The escapement: steel tooth on steel pallet, drop then lock. Tick, then tock a shade lower.
The wooden case: the hollow knock that makes it a clock and not a relay.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A wristwatch held to the ear, to a grandfather clock in a hallway.

controls.label: Case
controls.hint: A bare movement, all click, or a resonant wooden case that knocks.

controls.label: Tick and tock
controls.hint: Two identical ticks, or a tick and a clearly lower tock.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: At your ear, or across a silent room.

patch.name: Motor starting
patch.description: A big workshop extraction fan motor switched on at the wall. 0 ms: the contactor slams in with a heavy clunk that rings its steel cabinet; the motor lurches from standstill, growling under load, and climbs over 1.6 s to its running speed, the growl smoothing into a hum with a gear whine riding above it; it runs steadily for a moment, then fades as if you walked away.

tracks.note: The switchgear closing: a heavy relay clunk in a steel box.
The motor: from standstill to speed, load easing as it gets there.
The fan it drives: air building with the speed.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A desk fan to a ship's generator.

controls.label: Spin-up
controls.hint: Snaps up to speed, or takes its time getting a heavy flywheel moving.

controls.label: Age
controls.hint: New and smooth, or worn bearings that growl and wobble.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: A plain hum, or a gearbox that sings.

controls.label: Air
controls.hint: A bare motor, or one driving a big fan.

controls.label: Switch
controls.hint: A silent electronic start, or a contactor that slams.

patch.name: Ratchet
patch.description: A 3/8-inch socket wrench swung back on its ratchet in a garage, held close: fourteen teeth in about half a second, starting quick and slowing as the wrist runs out of swing. Each tooth is three things in 30 ms: the spring-loaded pawl drops off the tooth with a dry, bright steel tick (no note in it, a crowd of tiny partials gone in 10 ms), the forged head answers 1 to 3 ms later with a short dull knock around 400 to 900 Hz, and then the pawl rides up the next tooth with a faint greasy scratch. The hollow handle hums very slightly behind the clicks. Uneven the way a hand is; a little garage behind it.

tracks.note: The pawl snapping into each tooth: a 1.5 ms burst of bright noise through a tiny steel mechanism with a clustered chord of resonances, so every click is a dry dense tick, not a ping. Pitch and level wander from tooth to tooth.

The forged head and gear taking each blow: a small irregular lump of steel, heavily damped by the hand and the grease, landing 1 to 3 ms after the tick. The knock at 400 to 900 Hz that makes it a tool and not a toy.
The pawl riding up the next tooth against its spring: a few tiny greasy scratches between one click and the next. Quiet, but it is what makes the clicks a mechanism instead of a row of taps.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow deliberate click, click, click to a fast zip.

controls.label: Clicks
controls.hint: A short flick of three teeth to a long swing.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A watchmaker's ratchet to a winch on a boat: lower, heavier, longer knocks.

controls.label: Slow down
controls.hint: Even clicks like a machine, or a swing that runs out of travel.

controls.label: Handle
controls.hint: A solid, dead tool, or a hollow chrome handle that sings a little with each click.

controls.label: Grease
controls.hint: A dry, scratchy, chattering ratchet to a freshly packed one with duller, softer clicks.

patch.name: Servo move
patch.description: A hobby-size robot arm servo turning its joint through 90 degrees and stopping, heard close. 0 ms: the gear train takes up its slack with a small tick; the motor whines up to speed in 60 ms, buzzes steadily, then strains and drops in pitch over the last 100 ms as it brakes against the load; at 480 ms it stops dead with a plastic clack of the gears settling. Its small plastic case makes it nasal.

tracks.note: The geared motor: spins up, holds, strains as it brakes.
The gears landing at the end of travel: a small hard plastic clack.
Backlash taken up at the start: a tiny tick.

controls.label: Travel
controls.hint: A small twitch to a long sweep of the arm.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow precise crawl to a fast snap: higher whine.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A micro servo in a toy to an industrial arm joint.

controls.label: Strain
controls.hint: Moving nothing, or fighting a heavy load: rougher, buzzier.

controls.label: Stop
controls.hint: A soft controlled stop, or slamming into the end stop.

patch.name: Spring boing
patch.description: A doorstop spring flicked with a toe: the cartoon boing. 0 ms: the coil is bent and let go with a metallic twang; it whips back and forth so the pitch wobbles widely about seven times a second, the wobble dying over 600 ms while the whole note sags a little; the coil's overtones run away sharp of the pitch and chirp, the way spring reverbs do; a short plastic thunk from the skirting board it is screwed to.

tracks.note: The spring: a very stiff string, so its overtones go sharp and chirp. The LFO is the coil whipping about.
The wall it is screwed to: a short dull thunk at the flick.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A ballpoint pen spring to a car suspension coil.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: A plain twang, or a wild whipping boing-oing-oing.

controls.label: Wobble speed
controls.hint: A slow drunken sway to a fast shiver.

controls.label: Coil
controls.hint: A tight wire that just twangs, to a loose slinky that chirps and splashes.

controls.label: Flick
controls.hint: A soft thumb to a hard fingernail: brighter twang.

patch.name: Toggle switch
patch.description: A chunky metal bat-handle toggle switch on an aluminium control panel, flipped up with a thumb, heard from the pilot's seat. 0 ms: the lever passes centre with a small dull plastic tick. 14 ms: the spring throws the contact home, a hard, dry, dense clack (a crowd of tiny steel resonances gone in 20 ms, with the contact bouncing once 3 ms later), not a ping. At the same moment the thin panel it is bolted to takes the blow and answers with a short, boxy, slightly tinny "tok" at 200 to 800 Hz that makes it sound mounted in something. Dry and close, like an aircraft cockpit.

tracks.note: The lever going over centre: the small dull pre-click, an irregular bit of plastic, heavily damped.
The spring-loaded contact landing and bouncing once: a tiny irregular steel part, 24 crowded modes, damped hard by its housing, so it is a dry clack. The Metal control lets it ring.
The panel the switch is bolted to: a thin damped sheet with 40 crowded modes (its lowest filtered off), hit through the switch body. The boxy tok that gives it a size.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A tiny slide switch to a big knife-switch breaker.

controls.label: Throw
controls.hint: A crisp short-travel click, or a long lazy lever with a gap between tick and snap.

controls.label: Panel
controls.hint: A bare switch in the hand, or one mounted in a hollow console that knocks.

controls.label: Metal
controls.hint: A soft plastic rocker, through a dry steel clack, to an all-metal toggle that rings.

patch.name: Cloth swish
patch.description: A cotton jacket sleeve as an arm swings out and back: two brushes of fabric on fabric, the first about 150 ms long and the answer 220 ms after it, softer, lower and shorter. Each is thousands of fibres catching, so it is grainy rather than a hiss, swelling and thinning away with the speed of the arm; under the fibres the coarser threads of the weave drag over each other, a dry, pitchless rasp at 500 Hz to 3 kHz that gives the cloth its body. Very close, dry.

tracks.note: The fabric: a dense cloud of tiny noise grains whose rate swells and dies with each move. Grain size is the coarseness of the cloth.

The threads of the weave dragging past each other: a fast scrape over a dead, lumpy, heavily damped surface (48 crowded modes that die in a few ms, so nothing rings and there is no note), a little lower on the way back. The dry rasp that makes it a jacket rather than paper or a hiss.

controls.label: Fabric
controls.hint: Silk, through cotton, to stiff canvas or leather: coarser, lower, louder weave.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow drag to a quick flick.

controls.label: Return
controls.hint: One move only, to a full back-and-forth.

controls.label: Layers
controls.hint: A single thin sleeve to a heavy coat or cape: denser rustle.

patch.name: Jump take-off
patch.description: A light runner in trainers and a tracksuit jumping straight up from the sprung wooden floor of a small gym (the same person and floor as "Soft landing"). 0 ms: the legs drive and the boards take the load through the heels, a dull, dense knock with no note in it. 45 ms: the weight rolls to the toes, a second, lighter knock. 35 to 140 ms: the rubber soles scrub and twist on the lacquer, a dry scuff with a short rising sneaker chirp in it as they let go. 40 to 260 ms: the body goes up through its own clothes, a grainy rustle of nylon that thins out as the feet leave, over a faint rush of air. No cartoon boing and no whoosh: the effort is in the push and the shoes.

tracks.note: The boards taking the push: a big damped wooden panel (64 crowded modes, its lowest ones filtered off) loaded over a few milliseconds, heel then toe. A dense knock at 100 to 400 Hz, not a drum.
Rubber soles scrubbing the lacquer as they twist off: a burst of dry, mid-pitched grains that thins out as the feet leave. With the chirp, this is what says trainers.

The sneaker squeak: rubber sticking and slipping on the lacquer about 900 to 1500 times a second for 70 ms, rising as the foot lets go. A voice source used as a friction oscillator (one pulse per slip) through the sole's own narrow resonances; jitter, shimmer and rasp keep it rubbery, not a whistle.
Tracksuit fabric as the body straightens and rises: a cloud of fine fibre grains that swells for 80 ms and thins away. Takes the place of the usual noise whoosh.
The air the body moves: a soft breath of noise under the cloth, rising a little. Kept well under everything else.

controls.label: Effort
controls.hint: A little hop to an all-out leap: a harder push on the boards, more scrub from the shoes, a longer rustle.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: What they jump from: gym boards, packed earth, a metal deck or concrete. The same choices as Soft landing.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A child to a heavy man in boots: lower, bigger knocks from the floor.

controls.label: Squeak
controls.hint: Dusty soles that only scuff, to clean rubber chirping on fresh lacquer.

controls.label: Clothes
controls.hint: Bare legs and a vest, to a rustling shell suit: finer and louder fabric.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dead and close, a small gym, or an empty sports hall answering.

patch.name: Soft landing
patch.description: The runner from "Jump take-off" coming back down on the same sprung gym floor, landing softly on the balls of the feet with the knees bent. 0 ms: the first forefoot, a padded slap of thick rubber sole and a dull, dense knock from the boards. 28 ms: the second foot, a little lower and quieter, so it is two feet and not one drum. 40 ms: the soles bite the lacquer with a short falling sneaker chirp and a dry scrub. 105 ms: the heels and the body's weight arrive, a lower, softer knock. 70 to 370 ms: the tracksuit catches up and settles. A small gym answers quietly.

tracks.note: The boards taking the body: the same damped wooden panel as the take-off (64 crowded modes, its lowest filtered off), hit by something soft and wide over about 10 ms. Ball of the first foot, the second 28 ms later and a little lower, then the heels and the weight at 105 ms. Dense knocks at 100 to 400 Hz, no drum note.
The trainers themselves: thick rubber soles slapping flat on the lacquer, a dead, crowded pat at 250 to 900 Hz under each forefoot. This is what carries the landing on small speakers.
The soles gripping and scrubbing a few millimetres as they take the weight: the same dry rubber-on-lacquer grains as the take-off, once under the forefeet and again, smaller, as the heels come down.

The same sneaker squeak as the take-off, the other way round: the soles skid a hair and bite as the knees absorb the drop, a short chirp falling from about 1300 to 850 Hz at 40 ms. A voice source used as a stick-slip oscillator.
The tracksuit catching up with the body: the same fine fibre grains as the take-off, arriving as the knees bend and settling over a quarter of a second.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A child to a heavy man in boots: lower, bigger knocks and more heel.

controls.label: Softness
controls.hint: A flat-footed slap, to a cat-like landing where the knees take everything.

controls.label: Floor
controls.hint: What they land on: gym boards, packed earth, a metal deck or concrete. The same choices as Jump take-off.

controls.label: Feet
controls.hint: Both feet together, to one clearly after the other.

controls.label: Squeak
controls.hint: Dusty soles that only scuff, to clean rubber chirping on fresh lacquer.

controls.label: Clothes
controls.hint: Bare legs and a vest, to a rustling shell suit: finer and louder fabric.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dead and close, a small gym, or an empty sports hall answering.

patch.name: Fast whoosh
patch.description: A thin bamboo cane swung hard past the ear, 180 ms from start to stop: the air tearing along its length (a hiss that sweeps up to 5 kHz at the fastest point, 80 ms in, and back down) and the whistle of the tip itself, a narrow tone that rises and falls with the speed as the air sheds off the rod. Dry, close, no room.

tracks.note: The turbulence along the cane: band noise whose pitch follows the speed of the swing. The body of the whoosh.
