The whistle of the tip (the aeolian tone of a thin rod): a tube resonance that sweeps with the speed. It makes the swing thin and fast, not a gust.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A lazy swing to a whip-fast cut: shorter and higher.

controls.label: Thickness
controls.hint: A whip or a blade, to a staff or a bat: lower and broader.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: Plain rushing air to a singing edge.

patch.name: Heavy whoosh
patch.description: Something the size of a wrecking ball swinging past your head at 18 m/s, closest at 450 ms and a metre away: a low pressure wave you feel before you hear it, the roar of displaced air combing against itself as it passes (the hollow, jet-like sweep), and the pitch of everything sagging as it goes away. Gone by one second.

tracks.note: The displaced air: pink noise through a resonant comb that sweeps (the turbulence interfering with itself), then moved past the listener.
The weight: a fluttering low thrum at 100 to 300 Hz that swells as the object passes. Remove it and the whoosh becomes light.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A swung sandbag to a passing truck: more low thrum, darker air.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow, looming pass to a violent one.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Passing across the room to grazing your hair.

controls.label: Hollowness
controls.hint: Plain rushing air to a resonant, jet-like sweep.

patch.name: Cave drip
patch.description: Deep in a limestone cave, water gathers on a stalactite and falls two metres into a still pool: three drops (at 0, about 0.7 and 1.5 s, the gaps never equal), no two the same size. Each is a small wet slap on the surface, the "plink" of the bubble it drags under (its pitch flicking upward as the bubble closes) and, 60 ms later, the smaller droplets it threw up landing around it. The cave answers each one with an echo off the far wall 280 ms later and a long dark wash.

tracks.note: The bubble each drop drags under: a short ring whose pitch rises within 30 ms. Every drop is a different size, so a different note (up to a fourth apart) and level: three equal plinks read as a sonar.
The droplets thrown up by the impact, landing 60 ms behind each drop: a handful of smaller, higher bubbles. They share the drop's timing, so they stay attached to it at any rate.
The slap on the water surface: 30 ms of wet noise at each impact, a few ms ahead of the bubble. It is what makes the plink water and not a tone.

controls.label: Drop size
controls.hint: A fine bead to a fat, heavy drop: lower and rounder.

controls.label: Rate
controls.hint: A slow, patient drip to a quick trickle.

controls.label: Cave size
controls.hint: A wet cellar to a vast cavern: longer tail, later echo.

controls.label: Depth
controls.hint: Beside the pool to far down the tunnel: the echo takes over from the drop.

controls.label: Splash
controls.hint: A clean plink to a messier drop with droplets scattering.

patch.name: Crackling fire (loop)
patch.description: A campfire of dry pine an arm's length away: the soft low flutter of the flames, a steady fine crackle from the embers, sharp resin pops a few times a second with a little wooden knock in each, and now and then a hiss of sap. A 5 s loop; the flames and pops are random, and the end is crossfaded into the start over 0.5 s.

tracks.note: The flames: low noise that flutters irregularly at 8 to 12 times a second, as burning gas does. The warmth and the size of the fire.
The fine crackle: dense tiny pops with very uneven levels. The texture that says "fire" on any speaker.
Resin pockets bursting: sharp ragged pops, a few a second, some much louder than the rest.
The logs themselves cracking: small wooden knocks under some of the pops, so the fire is made of wood.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A candle-sized flame to a roaring bonfire.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: Glowing quietly to spitting and snapping.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Face in the heat to across the camp: the crackle softens, the flutter stays.

controls.label: Wood
controls.hint: Damp, hissing logs to bone-dry kindling: sharper, brighter pops.

patch.name: Rain (loop)
patch.description: Steady rain in a garden, heard from under a porch roof: thousands of small drops ticking on leaves and gravel (the bright patter), fat drops from the gutter plopping into a puddle a few times a second, and the far wash of rain on the whole street behind them. A 6 s stereo loop; nothing in it is periodic, and the end is crossfaded into the start over 0.6 s.

tracks.note: The near drops: separate ticks, each with its own pitch and place. This is what makes it rain and not hiss.
Heavy drops falling from the gutter into standing water: rising-pitch plops, sparse and louder.
All the rain you cannot pick out: a soft band of noise that breathes slowly. It fills the gaps between ticks.

controls.label: Intensity
controls.hint: A light drizzle to a downpour.

controls.label: Drop size
controls.hint: Fine mist to big heavy drops: lower, longer ticks.

controls.label: Puddles
controls.hint: Dry ground to water standing everywhere.

controls.label: Shelter
controls.hint: Out in it, to behind a closed window.

patch.name: Water splash
patch.description: A rock the size of two fists thrown into a pond from the bank, four metres away. The flat slap as it breaks the surface and the roar of water thrown aside; from 60 ms the hollow "gloop" of the air pocket closing behind it, a rough double gulp whose pitch climbs as the cavity shrinks, buried in the wash; the hissing crown of water going up and falling over most of a second, and its droplets raining back from 200 ms to past 1 s, big ones first, fine spray last. Open air, a short reflection from the far bank.

tracks.note: The surface breaking and the water thrown aside: a hard broad burst that darkens over 250 ms. It tells how flat and how fast the thing hit.

The cavity collapsing under water: a low rough gulp at 150 to 400 Hz whose pitch climbs, then a smaller second pocket 70 ms later. Noise-driven and half hidden by the wash, so it is turbulence, not a note. The weight of the splash, in the range small speakers have.
The sheet of water thrown up and falling back: a broad wash of noise that opens in 40 ms and dies away over 900 ms. The body of the splash.
The water coming back down: a shower of drops with rising pitch, the heavy ones first. Dense enough that they cannot be counted.
The fine spray: hundreds of tiny ticks at 3 to 9 kHz pattering onto the surface around the crown, thinning out by 800 ms.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A pebble to a boulder (or a body): deeper gloop, longer rain of drops.

controls.label: Impact
controls.hint: Slipping in edge-first to a flat, stinging belly flop.

controls.label: Spray
controls.hint: A clean plunge to a wide, hissing crown and a shower of droplets.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: At your feet to across the lake.

patch.name: Stream (loop)
patch.description: A shallow brook running over stones in a wood, heard from the bank: hundreds of small bubbles a second gurgling between the stones (each a little rising note between 300 Hz and 2 kHz), a deeper, slower glug where the water drops into a hollow, and the soft continuous hiss of the riffle. A 6 s stereo loop; everything is random, and the seam is crossfaded over 0.6 s.

tracks.note: The gurgle: a dense cloud of rising-pitch bubbles spread across the stream. The voice of the water.
The hollow under a small fall: big slow bubbles, 6 to 9 a second, in the 150 to 400 Hz range. Gives the stream depth.
White water over the shallow stones: an airy hiss that shifts slowly, so the bubbles sit in moving water.

controls.label: Flow
controls.hint: A trickle after a dry week to a brook in full spate.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A finger-wide rivulet to a wide, deep stream: lower, rounder bubbles.

controls.label: Pools
controls.hint: Flat shallows to deep hollows that glug.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Feet in the water to somewhere through the trees.

patch.name: Thunder
patch.description: Lightning strikes about 600 m away over open country. The crack arrives first: a tearing, splitting burst of 350 ms. Then the clap of the main channel at 120 ms, a hard dark slam that is over within a second, and after it the thunder rolls on for five seconds as sound from the farther parts of the bolt arrives: three more claps (near 0.9, 1.7 and 2.8 s), each softer, later and darker than the last, heaving up out of a grumbling bed that sinks to a low murmur.

tracks.note: The tearing crack of the near part of the bolt: a ragged cluster of sharp pops, not a single click. Only present when the strike is close.
The first clap: dark noise that slams in at 120 ms and is mostly gone in a second, leaving room for the roll. Kept strong from 80 to 300 Hz so it is felt on small speakers.

The later claps: the same slam from farther up the channel, arriving at about 0.9, 1.7 and 2.8 s. Each swells in over 60 to 150 ms instead of slamming, and is quieter and duller than the one before. They are what makes it thunder and not an explosion.
The bed the claps ride on: a grumbling, uneven rumble that heaves under each clap and sinks over five seconds.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Right overhead (all crack) to a storm beyond the hills (all rumble).

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: A small bolt to one that shakes the windows.

controls.label: Roll
controls.hint: One clap and done, to claps that keep coming and a rumble that goes on and on.

controls.label: Tear
controls.hint: A single snap to a long ripping crackle before the boom.

patch.name: Wind (loop)
patch.description: Wind over an open hillside with a hut on it: a broad rush of air that swells and falls in gusts every few seconds, a low buffeting underneath when it leans on the walls, and a thin whistle where it gets through a gap in the window frame, rising when the gust does. An 8 s stereo loop; the gusts repeat exactly once per loop (they are tied to 1/8 Hz and its multiples) and the seam is crossfaded over 1 s.

tracks.note: The air itself: pink noise whose colour and level rise and fall together with the gusts (one slow, one twice as fast, both whole cycles per loop).
Pressure on the walls and in the ears: slow, irregular low thumping between 60 and 200 Hz. The weight of the wind.
The gap in the window frame: noise ringing in a narrow tube, its pitch pushed up by each gust. The detail that gives the wind a voice.

controls.label: Strength
controls.hint: A breeze to a gale: brighter, fuller and heavier on the walls.

controls.label: Gusts
controls.hint: An even, steady blow to wild surges and lulls.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: Open country with nothing to whistle through, to a howling gap.

controls.label: Gap
controls.hint: The pitch of the whistle: a wide crack that moans, to a keyhole that shrieks.

patch.name: Bounce
patch.description: A ball bouncing in a 16-bit console game, on its two-operator FM chip. Each bounce is a rubbery boing: the pitch dips from 330 to 150 Hz in 40 ms as the ball squashes and springs back up past 400 Hz, while the FM index flares and relaxes. Three bounces, each sooner and quieter than the last, through the console's slightly grainy converter.

tracks.note: One squash and rebound, repeated as the ball settles.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A beach ball to a marble.

controls.label: Bounces
controls.hint: One boing to a ball that keeps going.

controls.label: Rubber
controls.hint: A dull round ball to a twangy, brassy one.

controls.label: Springiness
controls.hint: A dead ball that stops fast to a lively one with long, even hops.

patch.name: Coin
patch.description: A coin picked up on an 8-bit console with two pulse channels. One 50% square plays B5 for 70 ms and jumps a fourth to E6, which fades for 400 ms through the chip's 16 volume steps. No attack, no vibrato, nothing else: the jump is the reward.

tracks.note: The only channel: a square that steps up once and decays.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big gold coin to a tiny gem.

controls.label: Jump
controls.hint: How far the second note leaps: a minor third to an octave and a fifth.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A quick blip to a long ringing coin.

controls.label: Duty
controls.hint: A thin, nasal 12.5% pulse to a full hollow square.

patch.name: 8-bit explosion
patch.description: Something blows up on an 8-bit console. The noise channel starts at a fast clock (bright hiss) and is stepped down to a slow one over 700 ms, so the roar sinks into a rattling grumble, while its volume falls through all 16 levels, 50 ms each. The triangle channel adds the only bass the machine has: a rumble sliding from 120 to 50 Hz that jitters at random.

tracks.note: The blast: clocked noise whose clock slows, with a staircase fade.
The weight: a stepped triangle sliding down and shaking.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A popped crate to a boss going up: longer and deeper.

controls.label: Rumble
controls.hint: Noise alone to a blast with a shaking bass under it.

controls.label: Grumble
controls.hint: A smooth hiss that just fades to one that breaks up into rattling chunks.

controls.label: Crunch
controls.hint: A cleaner 6-bit machine to a brutal 2-bit one.

patch.name: Hurt
patch.description: The player takes a hit on an 8-bit console. The noise channel cracks for 50 ms while a thin 12.5% pulse drops more than an octave in 130 ms, its pitch thrown up and down 45 times a second so it sounds scrambled rather than sung. Cut dead at 140 ms. Harsh and short, as damage should be.

tracks.note: The pain: a falling pulse with a violent square wobble.
The impact: the noise channel at a low clock rate, so it is gritty, not hissy.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big boss grunt to a small critter squeal.

controls.label: Shake
controls.hint: A plain falling tone to a scrambled, glitching one.

controls.label: Crack
controls.hint: Only the yelp to a hard noisy smack on the front.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A quick flinch to a long, sinking defeat.

patch.name: Jump
patch.description: A character jumping on an 8-bit console. A 25% pulse sweeps up an octave and a half in 190 ms, its volume stepping down as it goes, and the noise channel spits a 25 ms scuff at take-off for the feet leaving the ground. It is cut off, not faded: the channel is needed for the next sound.

tracks.note: The jump: pitch is height.
Take-off: one short burst from the noise channel.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A heavy hero to a tiny, springy one.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: A small hop to a huge leap: how far the pitch climbs.

controls.label: Duty
controls.hint: A thin, nasal 12.5% pulse to a full hollow square.

controls.label: Feet
controls.hint: A clean synthetic jump to one that kicks off the ground.

patch.name: Laser
patch.description: A shot from a home-computer sound chip with a real filter. A pulse falls from 2.1 kHz to 260 Hz in 140 ms while its width opens from a thin sliver to a square, and the chip's resonant low-pass closes behind it. The player routine retriggers it twice more, quieter each time, 70 ms apart: the cheap echo of the era. Low sample rate leaves metallic aliasing on top.

tracks.note: The shot and its two software echoes.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A heavy cannon to a small pea-shooter.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A long descending beam to a quick pew.

controls.label: Echo
controls.hint: A single dry shot to three that trail off down a corridor.

controls.label: Squelch
controls.hint: A plain pulse to a wet, whistling filter sweep.

controls.label: Grit
controls.hint: A clean chip to a cheap one that rings and aliases.

patch.name: Menu select
patch.description: The cursor moving in an 8-bit menu, played on the triangle channel, which has no volume control: it is either on or off. A 16-step triangle at 660 Hz for 35 ms, then an octave up for 45 ms, switched off dead. The staircase of the 4-bit wave gives it a faint buzzing edge that a clean triangle does not have.

tracks.note: One channel, two pitches, no envelope.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Move it per menu row, or drop it for a back sound.

controls.label: Leap
controls.hint: A flat double blip to a jump of an octave and a fifth.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A tick to two clear notes.

controls.label: Steps
controls.hint: A buzzing 4-level staircase to a smooth, flute-like triangle.

patch.name: 1-up
patch.description: An extra life on an 8-bit console: a six-note rising figure on the first pulse channel, 80 ms a note, each note re-struck by a volume ramp, the last one held and faded. The second pulse channel plays the same line 80 ms late with a thinner duty and less volume, the trick old games used for echo when they had no reverb.

tracks.note: The tune.
The same tune one note late on the other channel: a fake echo.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Transpose the jingle to your game's key.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A stately fanfare to a quick sparkle.

controls.label: Echo
controls.hint: One dry channel to a full two-channel echo.

controls.label: Pluck
controls.hint: Smooth organ-like notes to sharply struck ones.

controls.label: Duty
controls.hint: A thin, nasal lead to a full hollow square.

patch.name: Power-up
patch.description: A power-up taken on an 8-bit console. One pulse channel cannot play chords, so it runs a major arpeggio at three notes every tenth of a second and walks it up the scale: six climbing triads in 630 ms, the last one held with a fast square vibrato. The triangle channel doubles the root of each triad two octaves down as a bass.

tracks.note: The arpeggio: fast enough to blur into rising chords.
The triangle channel: fixed volume, the root of each triad.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A weighty armour upgrade to a tiny speed boost.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow, grand fanfare to a quick zip upward.

controls.label: Duty
controls.hint: A thin, nasal 12.5% pulse to a full hollow square.

controls.label: Bass
controls.hint: The arpeggio alone to a full two-channel fanfare.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: A steady last note to a wide, warbling one.

patch.name: Console power-up
patch.description: An old bridge console is switched on. 0 ms: a contactor slams in (steel on steel). 20 ms: the degauss coil shudders, a 100 Hz buzz that shakes hard and dies away over 600 ms. From 80 ms the cooling fan spins up from standstill to speed, straining at first. From 500 ms the logic comes alive: a stutter of start-up self-test glitches that clears as it stabilises. At 1.35 s the system is up and says so with a soft, slightly detuned open fifth that fades into the fan noise.

tracks.note: Mains thrown in: hard, metallic, the first thing you hear.
The coil shudder old tubes make at switch-on: a buzzing 100 Hz saw that wobbles in level and dies. This is the weight.
The fan getting up to speed: load is high while it accelerates, then it settles.
Logic waking: corrupted bytebeat that gets cleaner (chaos falls) as the system finds its feet.
Up and running: a calm fifth, each partial doubled a few cents apart so it glows instead of beeping.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A handheld waking up to a whole engine room coming on line.

controls.label: Shudder
controls.hint: The coil buzz at switch-on: a faint hum to a cabinet-shaking thump.

controls.label: Fan
controls.hint: Silent solid-state gear to a loud whirring cooling fan.

controls.label: Self-test
controls.hint: A clean start to a long stutter of boot garbage.

controls.label: Ready tone
controls.hint: No chime, or a clear glowing 'online'.

patch.name: Computer data chirps
patch.description: A starship console working something out, heard through its small panel speaker. Eleven short bursts of data in about a second, uneven like a teletype: each is a slice of an integer bytebeat formula at a different pitch, so they are little broken melodies rather than beeps. Between them a relay ticks. At 1.15 s the answer arrives: two clean notes, up a fourth.

tracks.note: The thinking: bytebeat slices. Every event has its own randomness, pitch and length.
Hardware behind the panel: gives the bursts a machine to live in.
The result: the only clean, pitched thing, so it reads as 'done'.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow, pondering mainframe to a frantic burst of traffic.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big old low-voiced machine to a tiny chirpy droid.

controls.label: Corruption
controls.hint: Tidy patterns to skipping, stuttering, bit-flipped garbage.

controls.label: Answer
controls.hint: No result tone at all, or a clear two-note 'done'.

controls.label: Panel speaker
controls.hint: Clean and direct to a cheap buzzing speaker in a metal box.

patch.name: Force field hum (loop)
patch.description: Standing a metre from a containment field across a doorway, a 4 s seamless loop. The field's emitters hum at 58 Hz with a hollow, mostly odd set of harmonics that reach up to 2 kHz with a rasping edge, slowly breathing through a phaser as the field ripples. Its metal frame sings faintly along. Over the hum the surface of the field fizzes like a power line in rain, a hiss chopped 117 times a second. Somewhere inside, an unstable current wanders and flips (a gritty buzzing that never repeats), and a few times a second dust touches the field and pops.

tracks.note: The hum: weight at 58 to 290 Hz so it survives small speakers, and a buzzing edge of harmonics up to 2 kHz, roughened at twice the hum's frequency. The phaser runs exactly two cycles per loop.
The unstable current: a Lorenz attractor flipping between two lobes, overdriven so it buzzes and spits. This is what makes it dangerous instead of a fridge.
Dust and moths meeting the field: pops with ragged tails, a few a second, uneven in size.
The surface of the field: corona hiss above 2.5 kHz, chopped at twice the hum's frequency the way a high-voltage line fizzes. It puts the sound on a laptop speaker and says electricity, not motor.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A deep generator drone to a higher, tenser hum.

controls.label: Instability
controls.hint: A healthy steady field to one that buzzes and spits, about to fail.

controls.label: Edge
controls.hint: Soft and dull behind glass to bright, buzzing and close.

controls.label: Ripple
controls.hint: How deeply the field breathes.

patch.name: Blaster bolt
patch.description: A heavy plasma blaster fired down a ship's corridor. 0 ms: the capacitor snaps, a 15 ms digital crack. 2 ms: the bolt leaves, an FM tone whose pitch and sidebands collapse together (a 'bwow' from 1.9 kHz to 150 Hz in 220 ms), slightly overheated. 15 to 200 ms: sparks spit off the muzzle, each a tiny falling chirp. The steel corridor answers with a short ringing slap.

tracks.note: The capacitor letting go: the first 15 ms, stepped digital noise so it reads as electric, not as gunpowder.
The bolt itself. The carrier falls while the modulator's ratio falls faster, so the timbre growls downward instead of just dropping in pitch.
Sparks off the muzzle after the shot: separate little chirps, not hiss.

controls.label: Caliber
controls.hint: Small sidearm pew to a heavy, low cannon bolt.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A quick stab to a long drawn-out bwooow.

controls.label: Heat
controls.hint: A clean beam to an overdriven, spitting one with more sparks.

controls.label: Corridor
controls.hint: Dry and close, or ringing down a long metal passage.

patch.name: Plasma charge-up
patch.description: A plasma cannon's coil charging for 1.6 s before it is ready to fire. Two unstable oscillators feed each other inside the coil: at first a low warm buzz, then as the charge builds they rise two octaves and begin to tear. A containment pulse throbs under it, slow at first and blurring into a buzz at the top. A thin capacitor whine climbs above everything. At 1.6 s the charge locks with a small relay tick and the coil rings out for a moment in the housing.

tracks.note: The charge itself: cross-modulated sines that climb and lose stability. The tremolo is the containment pulse speeding up.
Capacitor whine: the thin tone that tells you how full it is.
The relay that says ready, right as the rise ends.

controls.label: Charge time
controls.hint: A half-second snap charge to a three-second build.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A pistol cell to a ship's main gun: lower and heavier.

controls.label: Instability
controls.hint: A clean, controlled hum to a charge that tears and screams near the top.

controls.label: Pulse
controls.hint: How hard the containment field throbs.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: The thin rising capacitor tone: none to piercing.

patch.name: Power down
patch.description: The main breaker is pulled on a ship's deck and everything on it dies. 0 ms: the breaker handle, a heavy plastic-and-steel clack. From 60 ms the turbine generator, with nothing left to drive it, winds down like a stopping tape over 1.8 s: its whine and the hum of the lights fall together, slowing as they go, into a growl and then nothing. At 1.5 s a last relay drops out somewhere in the dark.

tracks.note: The cause: a hand pulling the handle. Short and dry, in front of everything.
The machine. It plays steadily; the varispeed is what stops it, so pitch and time slow together the way a real rotor does.
Mains hum of the lighting: the low body under the whine, dying on the same curve.
One last relay letting go: the full stop.

controls.label: Wind-down
controls.hint: A light that just cuts out to a huge rotor taking seconds to stop.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A desk gadget to a reactor hall: lower and heavier.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: Mostly low hum, or a screaming turbine on top.

controls.label: Switch
controls.hint: How loud the breaker and the last relay are.

controls.label: Deck
controls.hint: Dry and close to a ringing metal hall.

patch.name: Scanner sweep
patch.description: A hand-held sensor passed slowly over a wall and back, 1.5 s. The scanner's beam is heard as air ringing in a narrow tube whose length changes with the sweep: the hollow tone glides from 320 Hz up to 1.9 kHz at 750 ms and back down, fluttering 20 times a second like scan lines. At the top of the sweep, when the beam crosses something, the beam ducks for a moment and the device pings (a small glassy FM note, clear over the beam), and the ping echoes twice inside the device.

tracks.note: The sweep: noise ringing in a tube resonator whose pitch follows the hand. Odd harmonics make it hollow, which reads as a beam rather than a synth. It ducks 7 dB for a tenth of a second at the turn so the ping has a hole to land in.
The find: lands where the sweep turns round, about as loud as the beam. A hard glassy attack that mellows in 90 ms; the delay is the device's own little echo.

controls.label: Sweep speed
controls.hint: A slow careful pass to a quick flick.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big deep-scan unit to a small shrill one.

controls.label: Scan lines
controls.hint: A smooth beam to a hard, buzzing flicker.

controls.label: Focus
controls.hint: A breathy wide beam to a tight whistling one.

controls.label: Ping
controls.hint: Nothing found, or a clear echoing contact.

patch.name: Energy shield impact
patch.description: A shot stops against a personal energy shield. 0 ms: a spitting 'tzzsh' of discharge where the round is vaporised, and the field itself is struck: it behaves like a huge thin glass bowl, but a dented one whose ring is chopped by a square-wave ring modulator and overdriven, so instead of a bell it gives a snarling, beating electric clang that is mostly gone in half a second. 0 to 450 ms: the surface crackles outward from the hit as the charge spreads. Under it a low unstable buzz dips and recovers over 300 ms: the field bowing in and springing back.

tracks.note: The shield as an object: a dented glass bowl 2 m wide, its modes beating. The square ring modulator and the drive break every mode into a crowd of sidebands, so it has the bowl's wobble but no note you could sing: glassy, but not glass.

The field bowing in and springing back: the weight of the hit. Two sines modulating each other on the edge of chaos, dropping from 190 to 74 Hz and recovering, chopped at 52 Hz: an unstable electric buzz, not a clean 'bwom'.
The charge spreading across the surface from the point of impact: a shower of sharp pops that thins out over 450 ms.
The 'tzzsh' on the hit: stepped digital noise above 1.5 kHz that tears for 150 ms. The round turning into light; it also gives the hit the top end the bowl lacks.

controls.label: Shield size
controls.hint: A wrist buckler to a ship's deflector: lower, longer ring.

controls.label: Hit force
controls.hint: A glancing pebble to a cannon round: harder, brighter, with more flex.

controls.label: Charge
controls.hint: A plain dented bowl to a fully electric, snarling clang.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: A steady ring to a fast shimmering flutter.

controls.label: Crackle
controls.hint: Surface discharge: none to a shower.

patch.name: Teleport out
patch.description: Someone is beamed away from a quiet room. 0 to 900 ms: the body dissolves into a column of glittering grains of tone that thicken and climb from 700 Hz to 9 kHz. Under them a hollow chord of the transporter beam swells and swirls. At 950 ms the column is gone and the air it left behind claps shut: a soft dull pop, and the room rings for a moment.

tracks.note: The body coming apart: hundreds of small tonal grains whose range climbs. Density builds, then thins as there is nothing left.
The carrier beam: a hollow, odd-harmonic chord that opens up and is swirled by a phaser.
Air rushing into the space the body left: a dull, pitchless pop. Without it the sound has no ending.

controls.label: Beam time
controls.hint: A quick blink away to a slow, ceremonial dissolve.

controls.label: Glitter
controls.hint: A few sparse motes to a dense sparkling column.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A deep cargo transporter to a small, high personal one.

controls.label: Swirl
controls.hint: A steady beam to a fast, bubbling vortex.

controls.label: Pop
controls.hint: How hard the air claps shut at the end.

patch.name: Warp jump
patch.description: A starship jumps to light speed, heard from just behind it. 0 to 1.2 s: space is pulled in: the ring of a huge struck hull plate played backwards in a cathedral-sized reverb, swelling out of nothing, while the drive's chord is stretched upward two octaves through a jet-like flanger. 1.2 s: the jump, the loudest thing in the sound: a slammed low boom with a cracking front edge and a roar of torn air that falls from bright to dark in half a second. After it the ship is already gone: its wake tears away past you (noise with real Doppler at 140 m/s) and the boom rolls off into empty space for three seconds.

tracks.note: The suck-in: a metal plate hit, drowned in reverb, faded to nothing at exactly 1.19 s and then reversed, so it swells from silence over the whole build and stops dead at the jump.
The drive spooling: a stacked saw chord dragged up two octaves, faster and faster. The flanger's delay closes to almost nothing, like a jet passing.

The moment: a huge soft-struck membrane for the boom (weight at 60 to 200 Hz) with a crumbling 120 ms noise front, pushed into a tube for harmonics small speakers can play. It has to out-weigh the riser.
The hole being torn: a roar of noise on the jump that falls from 6 kHz to 400 Hz in 600 ms. It gives the boom a body above 250 Hz and joins it to the wake.
The ship leaving: the doppler puts the closest pass at the jump, so only the falling, receding half is heard.

controls.label: Power
controls.hint: A small courier's hop to a capital ship tearing a hole.

controls.label: Pull
controls.hint: How strongly space is sucked in before the jump.

controls.label: Wake
controls.hint: A clean vanish, or a long tearing whoosh as it leaves.

controls.label: Void
controls.hint: A dry thump to a boom rolling away through an enormous space.

patch.name: Cancel / back
patch.description: Never mind: two tines of a wooden thumb piano plucked with the flesh of the thumb, stepping down a minor third 75 ms apart, each damped by the hand so it does not sing. The thumb lands on the board with a small woody knock. Dry and unhurried; a step back, not a failure.

tracks.note: The two notes going down. Muted so they read as a gesture, not a melody.
The thumb landing on the wooden box: the material of the set.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Move the pair up or down to sit under your confirm sound.

controls.label: Drop
controls.hint: How far the second note falls: a small step to a fifth.

controls.label: Mute
controls.hint: Open ringing tines to a short choked thunk.

controls.label: Wood
controls.hint: How much of the wooden box knocks under the notes.

patch.name: Error buzz
patch.description: Not allowed: a small piezo buzzer in a plastic case sounds twice, 90 ms each with a 50 ms gap. Two rough FM tones a flattened fifth apart beat against each other so it reads as no without being loud, and the case gives it a boxy 1.1 kHz honk. Flat, short, stops dead.

tracks.note: Two self-modulating carriers a tritone apart: the buzz and its disagreement.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A low refusal to a higher, lighter nope.

controls.label: Harshness
controls.hint: A dull hum to a rasping buzzer.

controls.label: Clash
controls.hint: One plain tone to two that grind against each other.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: Two quick blips to two longer buzzes that almost join.

patch.name: Hover tick
patch.description: A pointer passing over an item: the pad of a finger brushing the rim of a thin glass. A breath of skin on the surface (15 ms of soft air around 3.5 kHz) and under it one small note near 1.8 kHz whose two glass overtones last about 10 ms; a 2 ms front so it never clicks, gone in 40 ms. The quietest sound of the kit, 8 dB under the others, because it plays most often.

tracks.note: The glass: three partials, the upper two dying in about 10 ms. Low enough to be a touch, not a beep.
The fingertip: a short puff of soft noise that makes it a touch on something and not a tone.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Step it up or down per item for a row that plays a scale.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A dry tick to a small ringing ping.

controls.label: Glass
controls.hint: A plain soft blip to a brighter, glassier touch.

controls.label: Softness
controls.hint: A crisp nail tap to a rounded, clickless fade-in.

controls.label: Touch
controls.hint: A bare glass note to mostly the brush of the fingertip.

patch.name: Mechanical click
patch.description: One key of a mechanical keyboard pressed home. The plastic stem snaps past the click leaf (a 2 ms broadband tick, bright and pitchless, at 0 ms), bottoms out on the plate 11 ms later (a lower, boxier knock around 520 Hz) and the coil spring under it answers with a thin metallic ping for 100 ms. Close, dry, on a desk.

tracks.note: The click leaf letting go: a small stiff plastic part, so many damped modes that it has no note.
The edge of the snap: 1.5 ms of bright air that makes it a tick and not a tap.
The stem hitting the plate: the weight of the key, a few ms after the snap.
The coil spring ringing after the hit: the tail that says metal inside plastic.

controls.label: Travel
controls.hint: A short laptop key to a deep, slow switch: the gap between the snap and the bottom.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A light keycap to a heavy one on a thick plate.

controls.label: Snap
controls.hint: A quiet linear switch to a loud clicky one.

controls.label: Spring
controls.hint: How much the spring pings after the key lands.

patch.name: Notification chime
patch.description: Something arrived: three small FM bells stacked in fifths, 110 ms apart, each struck bright and mellowing within a quarter second while it rings on for a second. A single quiet echo and a studio plate put it a little way off, so it asks for attention without startling.

tracks.note: The three notes: a strike whose overtones fade faster than the tone.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A deep door chime to a small phone ping.

controls.label: Pace
controls.hint: A quick flick of three notes to a slow, calm arpeggio.

controls.label: Brightness
controls.hint: Soft and round to a hard, glittering strike.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Short dry notes to long ringing ones.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: Right at the screen to across a quiet room.

patch.name: Panel close
patch.description: A panel sliding shut like a drawer on felt runners: an FM tone falls a fifth and loses its overtones over 160 ms, and at 165 ms the panel lands with a soft, padded thud near 170 Hz. The landing is what tells it apart from Panel open: this one arrives somewhere.

tracks.note: The panel moving: brightness and pitch falling together.
The stop: a padded box thud. Gives the sound an end and some weight.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A small tooltip to a full-screen sheet: lower, slower, heavier landing.

controls.label: Brightness
controls.hint: A dull hum to a reedy, buzzing slide.

controls.label: Thud
controls.hint: A panel that just fades out to one that lands firmly.

controls.label: Padding
controls.hint: Felt-lined and dead to a bare wooden knock.

patch.name: Panel open
patch.description: A panel unfolding into view: a soft synthetic tone that climbs a fifth and opens from dull to clear over 200 ms, pushing a breath of air outward ahead of it, then settles in a small room. Gentle and rounded; nothing lands.

tracks.note: The panel: harmonics that are let in as it opens, on a rising pitch.
Displaced air, rising with the tone: the size of the thing that moved.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A small tooltip to a full-screen sheet: lower and slower.

controls.label: Brightness
controls.hint: Muffled and felt-like to open and reedy.

controls.label: Rise
controls.hint: Almost level to a clear upward leap.

controls.label: Air
controls.hint: A pure tone to mostly a breath of air.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: Flat on the glass to a panel in a room.

patch.name: Slider detent
patch.description: One notch of a dial with a ceramic detent wheel: a hard, dry 2.3 kHz tick as the ball drops into the groove, with a tiny low bump of the knob in the fingers, over in 20 ms. Drive Position from the slider value and a drag plays a rising row of ticks.

tracks.note: The detent itself: a few ceramic modes, heavily damped.
The knob settling in the hand: two cycles of a low bump, felt more than heard.

controls.label: Position
controls.hint: Where on the slider: low end to high end, a little over an octave of ticks.

controls.label: Hardness
controls.hint: A rubbery soft stop to steel on ceramic.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: A dead tick to a small ringing tink.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A weightless tick to a knob with some mass behind it.

patch.name: Soft click
patch.description: A fingertip pressing a soft silicone button, heard from typing distance. The pad of the finger lands (a 2 ms dull pat of air), the rubber dome gives with a rounded, pitchless knock around 430 Hz, and it is over in 50 ms. Dry and close; the default tap for anything pressed hundreds of times.

tracks.note: The body: a small plastic skin giving way. Sets the size of the key.
Skin on the surface: 15 ms of dull air that makes it a finger and not a beep.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A wide space bar to a tiny keypad dot.

controls.label: Touch
controls.hint: A soft fingertip to a fingernail: more edge on the front.

controls.label: Body
controls.hint: Dead and damped to a hollow little knock.

controls.label: Skin
controls.hint: How much of the finger you hear on top of the key.

patch.name: Soft confirm
patch.description: A friendly yes: two small glass tumblers tapped with a felt stick, the second a fourth above the first and 85 ms later, answering it, and a little louder so the rise is what you remember. Each has the uneven partials of real glass and a slow shimmer; the felt gives a short warm bump under each note. A small bright room keeps them from sounding like a test tone.

tracks.note: The two glasses, C6 then F6; the second note is the answer and rings on after a finger stops the first.
The felt stick: a short octave-below bump that gives the notes weight on small speakers.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: Higher is lighter and more toy-like; lower is calmer.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: Two quick taps to a lingering chime.

controls.label: Shimmer
controls.hint: Plain glass to a slow, beating sparkle in a bigger room.

controls.label: Warmth
controls.hint: Thin and glassy to round and padded.

patch.name: Success flourish
patch.description: Done, and done well: a quick upward run over four bright harp strings (a major chord to the octave, 55 ms apart), the top note left ringing, and from 150 ms a sprinkle of glass dust that thins and climbs as it falls away. A studio plate holds it together. About a second and a half; for the end of a task, not every click.

tracks.note: The gesture: four plucked strings going up, each a little louder.
The reward: tiny glass pings after the run, rising and thinning.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A warm low strum to a bright music-box run.

controls.label: Sparkle
controls.hint: Just the harp to a shower of glass dust after it.

controls.label: Strings
controls.hint: Soft gut strings to hard bright wire.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: A short dry run to strings that sing on.

controls.label: Space
controls.hint: Dry and close to a wide, glowing plate.

patch.name: Swipe
patch.description: A card flicked sideways across a touchscreen: 180 ms of air that swells and rises in pitch as the finger accelerates, with a faint hollow whistle from the gap under the card. No click at either end; it starts from nothing and thins out.

tracks.note: The movement: a band of noise sweeping with the gesture.
A hollow pitch inside the air, so the direction is heard and not only felt.

controls.label: Direction
controls.hint: Rising for forward or open, falling for back or dismiss.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow drag to a quick flick.

controls.label: Brightness
controls.hint: A heavy sheet moving to a thin, airy flick.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: Plain air to a clear hollow pitch in it.

patch.name: Text blip
patch.description: One syllable of a small character talking, for dialogue that types itself out: a 55 ms voiced "eh" from a tiny throat, its pitch dipping a little as it stops. Trigger one per letter with variations and the Pitch and Vowel controls wander into babble.

tracks.note: The whole sound: a throat, not a beep, so each character can have a voice.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A low grumble to a high chirpy speaker.

controls.label: Vowel
controls.hint: ah, eh, ee, oh, oo: vary it per letter for babble.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A mouse to an ogre: the throat, not the pitch.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A clipped tick of a voice to a full syllable.

controls.label: Robot
controls.hint: A soft living voice to a pressed, whistling machine.

patch.name: Toggle off
patch.description: The same rocker switch as Toggle on, thrown off. The plastic latch lands lower and duller at 0 ms, and 6 ms later the indicator tone that rose for on falls a fifth in 60 ms, from 760 to 510 Hz, closing down as it goes, like the light behind the switch dying. Lower, shorter and rounder than Toggle on.

tracks.note: The switch landing: the plastic box of Toggle on, tuned down and hit softer, more thud than tick.
The state going out: the indicator tone of Toggle on, falling and dimming so it reads as off without looking.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big panel switch to a tiny checkbox.

controls.label: Fall
controls.hint: How far the tone drops: a small nod down to a full octave slump.

controls.label: Click
controls.hint: All tone to mostly the dull switch.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A choked blip to a tone that sinks slowly.

patch.name: Toggle on
patch.description: A small rocker switch thrown on. The plastic latch ticks over at 0 ms, and 8 ms later a soft indicator tone slides up a fifth in 55 ms and fades, like a light coming up behind the switch. Pairs with Toggle off.

tracks.note: The physical switch: a dry plastic tick that says something moved.
The state: a tone that rises, so it reads as on without looking.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A big panel switch to a tiny checkbox.

controls.label: Rise
controls.hint: How far the tone climbs: a nudge to a bright leap of an octave.

controls.label: Click
controls.hint: All tone to mostly the plastic switch.

controls.label: Length
controls.hint: A clipped blip to a tone that lingers.

patch.name: Warning ping
patch.description: Look here, now: a small brass desk bell rapped twice with a metal pen, 150 ms apart and just as hard the second time. A second, smaller bell a tritone above is struck with it, so the pair grinds instead of chiming, and neither is quite round, so the ring beats unevenly. Pressed forward so the ring is as present as the rap, short and close in a hard little room: tense and insistent, but not a buzzer.

tracks.note: The main bell: rim modes of a small brass bowl near A5, damped by the desk it sits on.
The tension: a smaller bell a tritone up, struck together with the first. Without it the sound is a polite chime.
The pen on the metal: 3 ms of bright contact so both raps are counted clearly.

controls.label: Pitch
controls.hint: A larger bell for a grave caution, a small one for a sharp ping.

controls.label: Tension
controls.hint: One plain bell to two bells grinding a tritone apart.

controls.label: Urgency
controls.hint: Two patient taps, the second softer, to a fast, even double rap.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: A bell held in the hand to one left to sing.

controls.label: Hardness
controls.hint: A fingertip to a steel pen.

controls.label: Wobble
controls.hint: Perfect bells to ones whose ring beats and wavers.

patch.name: Car passing by
patch.description: A family hatchback passing on a two-lane road at 70 km/h, heard from the pavement six metres from its path: the engine note climbs out of the distance, a four-cylinder at 2800 rpm, the tyres hiss on the asphalt louder than the engine as it draws level at 1.9 s, the whole sound drops a tone as it passes, and the exhaust is what you hear last. Left to right, stereo, four seconds.

tracks.note: The four-cylinder under light load, holding its speed. Its firing pulses are what the Doppler shift is heard on.
Rubber on asphalt: a broad hiss around 1 kHz, the loudest thing when the car is close.
The air the car pushes aside: a low buffeting rush that gives the pass its body.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: Rolling through a car park to flat out on a motorway: a quicker, deeper drop in pitch, higher revs, more tyre.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: A road across the field to standing on the kerb.

controls.label: Engine
controls.hint: A small city car, to a van, to a truck: bigger, lower, louder against the tyres.

controls.label: Wet road
controls.hint: Dry asphalt to a road running with water: a bright, spraying hiss.

patch.name: Engine idling (loop)
patch.description: An older four-cylinder petrol car idling at the kerb, bonnet shut, heard from beside the front wheel: 780 rpm, 26 firings a second with one cylinder a little weak so it lopes, the valve gear ticking lightly on top, and the exhaust burbling at the back. A 2 s loop that holds exactly 13 engine cycles (two turns each), crossfaded over 150 ms on a cycle boundary.

tracks.note: The firing pulses through the exhaust: the engine itself. Roughness is what makes it an old car and not a test tone.
Tappets: a light metallic tick at twice the firing rate (52 a second), slightly uneven. The mechanical top end you hear standing next to it.
Exhaust gas pulsing out of the tailpipe: low noise chopped at the firing rate, so the idle has breath as well as tone.

controls.label: Idle speed
controls.hint: A slow, lumpy tick-over to a fast, cold-start idle. (Away from the middle the loop relies on its crossfade.)

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A scooter-sized engine to a lorry diesel: lower pipe, heavier pulses.

controls.label: Wear
controls.hint: Fresh from the factory to a tired engine that misses and lopes.

controls.label: Tappets
controls.hint: Bonnet shut and quiet, to a noisy, ticking top end.

controls.label: Exhaust
controls.hint: A whisper-quiet silencer to an open, burbling pipe.

patch.name: Helicopter (loop)
patch.description: A light two-blade helicopter in a hover 150 m away: the main rotor slapping ten times a second (300 rpm), the tail rotor buzzing at 80 Hz with a hard edge just above it, the downwash hissing in time with the blades, and the turbine only a faint, breathy whine far behind them, chopped by the passing blades and dulled by the air in between. A 2 s stereo loop holding exactly 20 blade slaps, crossfaded over 200 ms.

tracks.note: The main rotor: two blades at 300 rpm, a slap every 100 ms. The "wop-wop" that is the whole character.
The tail rotor: four small blades at 1200 rpm, an 80 Hz buzz with a hard edge. Heard most from the side.

The engine: mostly hiss, with a faint whine that drifts a few cents, is chopped ten times a second by the blades passing in front of it and is dulled by 150 m of air. It sits well under the rotors: it separates a helicopter from a big fan without ever being a whistle.
Downwash: air noise that pulses with each blade passing, the soft part of the slap.

controls.label: Distance
controls.hint: Standing under the disc to a speck on the horizon: only the thump of the blades carries.

controls.label: Size
controls.hint: A two-seat trainer to a heavy-lift transport: slower, deeper blades.

controls.label: Strain
controls.hint: Idling on the pad to hauling a load in a hard turn: louder, harsher slaps.

controls.label: Turbine
controls.hint: No engine to hear at all, a faint whine behind the rotors, or a jet turbine screaming over them.

patch.name: Jet fly-by
patch.description: A fighter jet crossing low over an airfield at 120 m/s, 250 m up: almost nothing until it is on you, the compressor whine arriving first and thin, then at 1.9 s the pass, and behind it the real sound: the tearing, crackling roar of the exhaust that drops in pitch and takes four seconds to roll away, hollowed by its reflection off the runway. Left to right, stereo, six and a half seconds.

tracks.note: The compressor: a thin whistle you hear from the front, fading as the jet shows its tail.
The exhaust: broadband roar that is quiet in front of the jet and enormous behind it, with the comb of the ground reflection sweeping as the angle changes.
The low end of the exhaust: a rumble from 80 to 250 Hz that arrives with the pass and outlasts everything.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: An airliner on approach to a fast, hard military pass: the onset gets more sudden.

controls.label: Height
controls.hint: Skimming the runway to high overhead: a slower, gentler swell.

controls.label: Afterburner
controls.hint: Throttled back and whistling, to full reheat: crackle, distortion and low thunder.

controls.label: Whine
controls.hint: How much compressor whistle leads the roar.

controls.label: Ground
controls.hint: Open sky to a hard runway under it: the hollow sweep in the roar.

patch.name: Motorbike rev
patch.description: A rider on a big V-twin at a red light, blipping the throttle: off the idle (1100 rpm) a first short blip to 4500 at 250 ms, back down, then a longer, harder one to 6800 at 1.0 s that hangs for a moment before the revs fall, pop and burble on the overrun and settle back into the lumpy idle by 2.3 s. Open pipes, a street with buildings on both sides.

tracks.note: The twin: two cylinders firing unevenly, revs and load drawn by hand so the throttle leads and the engine follows.
Unburnt fuel popping in the pipes as the throttle shuts: a scatter of sharp cracks from 1.25 to 1.9 s.
The carburettors gulping air on each twist of the throttle: a short rising rush under each blip.

controls.label: Revs
controls.hint: A gentle twist of the wrist to bouncing it off the limiter.

controls.label: Bike
controls.hint: A buzzing 125, a mid-size twin, to a big slow cruiser.

controls.label: Pipes
controls.hint: A legal, muffled silencer to straight-through open pipes.

controls.label: Pops
controls.hint: A clean engine to one that bangs and crackles when the throttle closes.

controls.label: Wear
controls.hint: A tight, even engine to a loose old one.

patch.name: Bow shot
patch.description: A longbow loosed beside your ear in a wood: 'thwp-fff', not a note. 0 ms: the fingers let go and the string snaps forward, a short dry thrum around 150 Hz with its buzz on top. 3 ms: the limbs kick forward and stop, a dull crowded wooden knock in the stave. 18 ms: the string reaches the end of its travel and slaps the bracer, a flat leathery smack that chokes the thrum within 100 ms. From 12 ms the arrow is away: a breathy hiss with fletching flutter that falls in pitch and fades over 400 ms as it flies off at 55 m/s. The trees give back a soft, short scatter.

tracks.note: The bowstring: a real waveguide string let go near its middle, stiff and buzzy, choked by the mute curve the way the bracer and the limbs stop it. A thrum, over in a tenth of a second, with the bass cut so it never reads as a bass note.
The string smacking the bracer at the end of its travel: a 20 ms flat slap of noise with a leathery low-mid body. This is the 'p' of 'thwp'.
The stave kicking in the hand: a damped wooden body with 40 crowded modes, hit over a few milliseconds. The 'thock' that makes it a bow and not a guitar.
The arrow in flight: a broad breathy hiss, fluttered by the fletching (fast tremolo), carried away by the doppler so it falls in pitch and fades.

controls.label: Draw weight
controls.hint: A light hunting bow to a heavy war bow: deeper thrum, harder kick, faster arrow.

controls.label: Twang
controls.hint: A well-silenced thump to a long buzzing string.

controls.label: Bracer slap
controls.hint: A clean release to the string cracking hard against the arm guard.

controls.label: Arrow
controls.hint: Just the bow, or a loud hissing shaft leaving it.

controls.label: Fletching
controls.hint: A smooth thin bolt to big fluttering feathers.

controls.label: Woods
controls.hint: An open field, dry, to deep among the trunks.

patch.name: Bullet fly-by
patch.description: You are being shot at across open ground and the round misses your head by a couple of metres: snap-zip, then, much later, the gun. 0 ms: the bullet is faster than its own sound, so the first thing you hear is its shock wave slapping your ear, a sharp dry crack, the thing that makes you duck. 10 to 200 ms: the zip of the round itself tearing away to the right, a ragged buzz inside a hiss of torn air (the spinning slug, never a clean whistle), its pitch falling most of an octave as it goes, gone in a fifth of a second. About a second later the rifle's own report arrives from 300 m away: a dull, low, pitchless thump with its top end eaten by the air, and a short roll off the ground and the tree line.

tracks.note: The shock wave, which reaches you before anything else: 10 ms, bright, dry, the loudest instant. This is what makes people duck.

The round in the air: a logistic map half-way into chaos, its rate wandering, is a ragged buzz rather than a tone. Steady by itself; the doppler does the motion, pitch drop and pan, and the envelope ends it a fifth of a second after the pass.
Torn air around the slug: plain hiss on the same path, the body of the zip.
The gun, late and far: a burst of dark noise whose top closes as it dies, driven a little so it is a thump of pressure and not a drum, then the slap off the ground and the trees.
The muzzle blast's low push under the report: a slack skin struck with a crumbling 60 ms hit, short and well under the noise so no note is heard.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Passing ten metres off, a soft zip, to parting your hair: sudden and vicious.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A lazy spent round to a supersonic rifle bullet: a bigger, quicker pitch drop.

controls.label: Buzz
controls.hint: A clean hiss of air to an angry, hornet-like tumbling slug.

controls.label: Shooter range
controls.hint: Fired from close by, loud and soon, or from far off: later, duller, quieter.

patch.name: Reload
patch.description: A service pistol reloaded in a quiet room, close to the microphone: dry, dense, damped clacks with steel sliding between them, nothing that rings. 0 to 55 ms: a full magazine rasps up the magazine well. 58 ms: it seats, the catch snapping over it 13 ms later, with the palm's thump on the polymer grip behind both. 300 to 430 ms: the slide is racked back, a 'shh' of steel on steel with the rails' machining ticking under it, slowing as the spring loads, and knocks its rear stop. 470 ms: let go, the slide runs home, the loudest hit: slide meeting barrel, then the lock-up 9 ms later, a chunky double clack with the frame's knock under it and the recoil spring chattering for a moment after.

tracks.note: The magazine sliding up the well: a short rising rasp of sheet steel on polymer, before the click.
Mag seating, then the catch snapping over it 13 ms later: a full steel box held in a hand, so 48 crowded modes, heavily damped, dented. A clack with no note in it.
The palm and the polymer grip taking the slap: the low half of the magazine's clack, 2 ms late.
The slide dragged back: the 'shh' of steel on oiled steel, falling in pitch as it slows, coloured by a very short metallic resonance so it is a gun and not paper.
The rails' machining and the disconnector riding over them: a loosely regular run of small steel ticks, slowing with the slide.

The slide's three knocks: its rear stop at the end of the rack (softer, higher), then home against the barrel 40 ms later and the lock-up 9 ms after that. A dense, dented steel box, 64 modes dead within 50 ms.
The frame and the hand taking the slide's mass as it stops: the knock under the slam that makes it a clunk and not a tick.
The recoil spring and loose parts chattering after the slam: a thinning burst of tiny dull steel ticks. Small, but it says 'mechanism'.

controls.label: Weight
controls.hint: A pocket pistol's ticks to a heavy rifle's clunks.

controls.label: Hands
controls.hint: A slow, deliberate reload to a fast practised one.

controls.label: Snap
controls.hint: Oiled and soft, a muffled clunk, to dry, hard and clacking.

controls.label: Slide
controls.hint: A barely heard rack to a long gritty drag of steel on steel.

controls.label: Looseness
controls.hint: A tight new gun, or a worn one whose spring and parts rattle after the slam.

controls.label: Room
controls.hint: Dead close-up foley to a bare concrete room.

patch.name: Ricochet
patch.description: A rifle bullet glances off a steel girder in a canyon and whines away. 0 ms: the strike, a hard bright tick on thick steel, and a puff of grit. 5 ms: the deformed slug tumbles off, and its spin sings: a wiry tone that starts at 3.6 kHz and slides down to 900 Hz over 700 ms, wobbling faster and faster as the tumble speeds up, flying away from you so it also dulls and fades. A single canyon echo repeats the whine, darker.

tracks.note: Lead on steel: tiny object, huge force. A small damped bar, struck as hard as possible.
The tumbling slug: a stiff bowed wire, not an oscillator, so the tone is ragged and has rushing air in it. The pitch falls; the wobble (the tumble) speeds up from 9 to 30 Hz.
Paint, rust and lead dust knocked off: a short burst of dry ticks. Places the hit on a real surface.

controls.label: Calibre
controls.hint: A small fast round's thin zing to a heavy slug's low moan.

controls.label: Whine length
controls.hint: A quick 'pting' to a long cartoon-western peeeoww.

controls.label: Tumble
controls.hint: A clean spinning zing to a wildly wobbling, deformed slug.

controls.label: Surface
controls.hint: What it hit.

controls.label: Canyon
controls.hint: No echo, or the whine coming back off far rock walls.

patch.name: Sword clash
patch.description: Two steel blades meet edge to edge in a stone courtyard: a harsh bite, a clank and a ring, not a chime. 0 ms: the edges bite, a 5 ms broadband crunch of steel on steel. With it the attacker's long blade is set ringing, struck near its tip and chattering twice more against the other edge over the next 30 ms: a bright, crowded, beating cluster of overtones from 1.5 to 8 kHz, with no single bell note under it. 4 ms: the defender's blade, gripped hard, answers with the clank, lower, dented and dead within a quarter of a second. 25 to 280 ms: the edges grind along each other to the guards, a gritty 'shing' that slows down. The walls give it a short hard slap, and the attacker's blade sings on for half a second.

tracks.note: The contact itself: 5 ms of clipped noise as the edges cut into each other. The harshness that makes it a blow, not a bell.

The swung blade: free to ring, struck near the end, then chattering twice against the other edge. 48 crowded, dented, beating modes with the bar's low note filtered away, so the ring is a shimmering cluster and not a chime bar.
The parrying blade: gripped hard, so it clanks and dies. Another object (other variant), 4 ms late; the flam is what makes it two swords, and its low-mids are the weight of the blow.
Edges grinding to the hilt, the 'shing': gritty scrape on a dented blade flat, ridge rate falling as the slide slows.

controls.label: Blade size
controls.hint: Daggers, thin and high, to great two-handers.

controls.label: Force
controls.hint: A light tap of blades to a full-strength blow with a harsh bite.

controls.label: Ring
controls.hint: Blades caught and deadened, a dry clank, or left singing.

controls.label: Slide
controls.hint: A clean bounce apart, or a long grind down to the guards.

controls.label: Courtyard
controls.hint: Open field, dry, to hard stone walls close by.

patch.name: Sword swing
patch.description: A longsword swung hard past your head, right to left, no contact. The blade is a thin edge moving at 30 m/s half a metre away: 280 ms of air being cut, a narrow whistle that rises as the blade comes and falls as it goes (real Doppler, not a filter sweep), loudest for only 60 ms in the middle. Under the whistle the flat of the blade pushes a duller gust. As it passes, the steel itself sings very faintly, the way a blade hums when it moves fast.

tracks.note: The cutting edge: noise through a tube resonator gives the whistle a pitch, and the doppler bends it past you. The story is in this layer.
The gust off the flat of the blade: lower and softer, a few ms behind the edge. Gives the swing weight.
The steel humming: a long bar excited by a faint scrape of air. Barely there; mute it and the swing becomes a stick.

controls.label: Speed
controls.hint: A slow heavy arc to a whip-fast cut: shorter and with a bigger pitch bend.

controls.label: Blade
controls.hint: A thin rapier's whistle to a broad greatsword's whump.

controls.label: Whistle
controls.hint: Plain rushing air to a sharp singing edge.

controls.label: Closeness
controls.hint: Across the room to shaving your ear: sharper and more sudden.

controls.label: Steel
controls.hint: A wooden practice sword to ringing steel.
